a nil exporter, or a distinct exporter claiming an already-registered Name.

symbols.name: CodeExportFailed
symbols.doc:
CodeExportFailed identifies an exporter that returned an error while shipping
a snapshot (the exporter's cause rides the wrap trail).

symbols.name: CodeInstrumentKindConflict
symbols.doc:
CodeInstrumentKindConflict identifies a Meter call reusing a name already
bound to a DIFFERENT instrument kind (e.g. a Counter name fetched as a Gauge,
or as an UpDownCounter, which is a different monotonicity on one metric).

symbols.name: CodeInvalidAttribute
symbols.doc:
CodeInvalidAttribute identifies an instrument fetched with an attribute set
that cannot name a series: an attribute with an empty Key, the same Key
twice, or a value no constructor ever set (AttrKindInvalid).

symbols.name: CodeInvalidDescription
symbols.doc:
CodeInvalidDescription identifies a Describe call carrying an empty
description — a call that would document nothing (ADR 0067).

symbols.name: CodeInvalidLabelName
symbols.doc:
CodeInvalidLabelName identifies an attribute key the Prometheus text
exposition format cannot carry: it does not match [a-zA-Z_][a-zA-Z0-9_]* (a
metric name may hold a colon, a label name may not — and neither may hold the
dot every OTel-conventional attribute key is spelled with).

symbols.name: CodeInvalidMetricName
symbols.doc:
CodeInvalidMetricName identifies an instrument name the Prometheus text
exposition format cannot carry: it does not match [a-zA-Z_:][a-zA-Z0-9_:]*.

symbols.name: CodeInvalidTemporality
symbols.doc:
CodeInvalidTemporality identifies a MeterConfig carrying a Temporality that
is none of the three declared constants — reachable only by a deliberate cast.

symbols.name: CodeOTLPEndpointInvalid
symbols.doc:
CodeOTLPEndpointInvalid identifies an OTLP/HTTP exporter configured with an
endpoint that is not an absolute http(s) URL carrying a path — the address
the POST would otherwise be sent to blind.

symbols.name: CodeOTLPExportRejected
symbols.doc:
CodeOTLPExportRejected identifies a collector that refused the payload
PERMANENTLY: an HTTP status outside the specification's retryable set, so
replaying the same bytes would fail the same way.

symbols.name: CodeOTLPExportUnavailable
symbols.doc:
CodeOTLPExportUnavailable identifies a TRANSIENT OTLP/HTTP failure — a
transport fault, or one of the four statuses the specification lists as
retryable. The same bytes may succeed later.

symbols.name: CodeOTLPInvalidBucketLayout
symbols.doc:
CodeOTLPInvalidBucketLayout identifies a histogram point whose buckets OTLP
cannot express: a count array that is not one longer than the bounds array,
or bounds that are non-finite or not strictly increasing.

symbols.name: CodeOTLPPartialSuccess
symbols.doc:
CodeOTLPPartialSuccess identifies a collector that accepted the request
(HTTP 200) but rejected some of its data points. The specification forbids
retrying it, so the loss is reported rather than replayed.

symbols.name: CodeOTLPUnresolvedTemporality
symbols.doc:
CodeOTLPUnresolvedTemporality identifies a snapshot handed to the OTLP/JSON
encoder carrying a temporality that is neither delta nor cumulative. The
schema's AGGREGATION_TEMPORALITY_UNSPECIFIED "MUST not be used", so there is
no honest integer to emit.

symbols.name: CodeReservedLabelName
symbols.doc:
CodeReservedLabelName identifies a syntactically legal attribute key that the
exposition format or the Prometheus server reserves for its own use: the "__"
prefix, or "le" on a histogram, where it names the bucket's upper bound.

symbols.name: CodeUnknownExporter
symbols.doc:
CodeUnknownExporter identifies an Export/Lookup naming an exporter that no
imported package has registered.

symbols.name: CodeUnsupportedTemporality
symbols.doc:
CodeUnsupportedTemporality identifies a snapshot that is not cumulative —
delta, or an unresolved temporality — handed to the Prometheus exporter,
whose exposition format has no temporality field and whose server reads
every counter as cumulative.

symbols.name: ContextExporter
symbols.spelled: interface{ExportContext(ctx context.Context, snap SnapshotValue) error; Exporter}
symbols.doc:
ContextExporter is an Exporter whose export can be bounded and cancelled:
ExportContext ships snap under ctx, and returns once ctx is done at the
latest. The OpenTelemetry metrics SDK specification bounds every export by
exportTimeout; Export has no context to bound it with, and Exporter is a
published port, so the bound arrives as this sibling rather than as a widened
method (ADR 0039). A caller holding an Exporter asks for it with a type
assertion, as ExportContext does.

Implementations MUST be safe for concurrent use, and Export keeps its
meaning: it is ExportContext under a context the exporter bounds itself.

symbols.name: Counter
symbols.doc:
Counter is a MONOTONIC sum: it only ever increases. In the OTel data model
its points land in a Sum carrying Monotonic = true, which is what tells a
backend that a decrease is a restart rather than a measurement.

symbols.name: Add
symbols.doc:
Add increments the counter by a non-negative delta. A non-positive
delta is ignored — a counter that could go down is an UpDownCounter,
and a backend reading this one is entitled to assume it cannot.

symbols.name: Inc
symbols.doc: Inc increments the counter by one (Add(1) shorthand).

symbols.name: DefaultExportTimeout
symbols.doc:
DefaultExportTimeout bounds one export when the caller's context carries no
deadline of its own: 30 s, the OpenTelemetry metrics SDK specification's
default exportTimeout for a periodic exporting reader
(OTEL_METRIC_EXPORT_TIMEOUT). A context with no deadline is how an
indefinite block is written; a caller who wants another bound puts it on the
context.

symbols.name: DefaultScopeName
symbols.doc:
DefaultScopeName names this SDK as the instrumenting library when a caller
declares no scope of their own. An empty scope name is legal in the
specification and useless in a backend, so the meter fills in the one thing
it can state truthfully: which library minted the instruments.

It is this signal's own constant and is deliberately not shared:
internal/core/observe/trace declares its own, because a scope names the library that
produced THIS signal (ADR 0051 §Decision 2).

symbols.name: Describer
symbols.doc:
Describer attaches a human-readable description to an instrument NAME.

The OTel metrics data model puts `description` on the Metric, not on the data
point, and the specification says outright that it is NON-IDENTIFYING: two
streams that differ only by their description are one stream. That is why
this is Describe(name, …) and not a description parameter threaded through
Counter/Gauge/Histogram. A description describes the thing a backend graphs,
which is the name; a call site only ever contributes one series of it, and a
per-call-site parameter would invite two call sites to disagree about the
documentation of one metric while both look correct.

It is also why the description is not on the observation path at all. Counter
and its siblings are called once per observation; Describe is called once, at
wiring time, next to the code that decides the instrument exists.

# A sibling, discovered by type assertion

Meter is FROZEN (ADR 0039) and so is FullMeter — a union is still an
interface, and adding a method to either would break every downstream double
at compile time with no deprecation window. Describer is therefore a fourth
sibling beside UpDownMeter and AsyncMeter, and it is NOT folded into
FullMeter:

	if d, ok := meter.(metrics.Describer); ok {
		d.Describe("http_server_requests", "Requests served, by route and status")
	}

The assertion is not ceremony. A Meter that records no description — a test
double, a no-op meter, a downstream implementation written before this port
existed — legitimately does not implement Describer, and `ok == false` is how
a caller finds out that their documentation will not reach the wire. The same
shape as cache.Tagger (ADR 0049) and lock.Deadliner (ADR 0052): the ABSENCE
of the sibling is the answer.

# What an implementation is expected to refuse

Both refusals are programmer errors — a description is a literal written at a
wiring site, constant for the process — so an implementation is expected to
refuse them LOUDLY rather than return an error this signature has nowhere to
put, exactly as Meter refuses a cross-kind name reuse:

  - An EMPTY description. It is a call that does nothing, which is the inert
    outcome ADR 0031 bans; the caller meant to write something.
  - A SECOND, DIFFERENT description for one name. A description belongs to
    the name, so two of them means one of the two wiring sites is wrong, and
    whichever one lost would be invisible on every wire. Re-describing a name
    with the SAME text is idempotent, because two packages documenting one
    metric identically have not disagreed about anything.

A description is DATA, not structure: unlike an instrument name or an
attribute key, it is prose, and an implementation must not refuse it for the
bytes it contains. An exporter escapes it for the wire it is writing.

symbols.name: Describe
symbols.doc:
Describe binds description to the instrument called name. It is
idempotent for identical text and refused for conflicting text.

symbols.name: DescriptionConflict

code.public: That instrument name already carries a different description

symbols.doc:
DescriptionConflict is the panic sentinel for two different descriptions
bound to one instrument name.

symbols.name: DocumentExporter
symbols.doc:
DocumentExporter is the sibling of ContextExporter an exporter implements
when it can ship a snapshot already encoded as its wire document:
ExportDocument sends doc under ctx, as ExportContext sends the snapshot it
would have encoded into it, with the same verdicts. The OTLP/HTTP
exporter implements it, doc being an OTLP/JSON
ExportMetricsServiceRequest — what EncodeOTLPJSON writes —, so a
snapshot encoded and stored by a store-and-forward queue is posted later
without being decoded (ADR 0185). An empty doc sends nothing.

A caller holding a ContextExporter asks for it with a type assertion
(ADR 0039). Implementations MUST be safe for concurrent use.

symbols.name: DuplicateRegistration

code.public: An exporter is already registered under that name

symbols.doc: DuplicateRegistration is the boot-time Exporter-registry panic sentinel.

symbols.name: Export
symbols.doc:
Export ships snap through the Exporter registered as name. A missing exporter
returns UnknownExporter; an exporter failure wraps as ExportFailed.

symbols.name: ExportContext
symbols.spelled: func(ctx context.Context, name ExporterName, snap SnapshotValue) error
symbols.doc:
ExportContext ships snap through the Exporter registered as name, bounded by
ctx. A missing exporter returns UnknownExporter; an exporter failure wraps as
ExportFailed.

When ctx carries no deadline, DefaultExportTimeout is applied: the
specification bounds every export. An exporter that implements ContextExporter
receives the bounded context through ExportContext; one that implements only
Exporter is called through Export, which has no context to honour, and is
bounded by nothing but itself — every exporter that touches a network in this
SDK implements the sibling.

symbols.name: ExportFailed

code.public: The metrics exporter failed to ship the snapshot

symbols.doc: ExportFailed wraps an exporter's failure while shipping a snapshot.

symbols.name: Exporter
symbols.doc:
Exporter ships a Snapshot to a backend (text writer, Prometheus, OTLP, …).
Implementations MUST be safe for concurrent use.

IFACE-PLUGIN: the registry stores plug-in exporters behind this interface;
concrete exporter types stay unexported per package.

symbols.name: ExporterName
symbols.doc:
ExporterName is the typed key under which an Exporter registers (e.g. "text",
"prometheus"). The zero value ExporterName("") is reserved invalid.

symbols.name: String
symbols.doc: String returns the raw name.

symbols.name: Float64Callback
symbols.doc:
Float64Callback is Int64Callback for a double-valued observable — an
observable gauge, whose reported value is a sampled reading and therefore has
no temporality at all.

symbols.name: FullMeter
symbols.doc:
FullMeter is the whole OTel instrument set behind one name: the frozen Meter
plus both siblings. It is what every constructor in this SDK returns, and
widening a returned VALUE from Meter to FullMeter is safe for the same reason
widening clock.System from Clock to Timed was — every existing assignment
into a Meter still compiles (ADR 0039 §Decision 1).

symbols.name: Gauge
symbols.doc: Gauge is an instantaneous value that can go up or down.

symbols.name: Add
symbols.doc: Add adjusts the gauge by delta (may be negative).

symbols.name: Set
symbols.doc: Set replaces the gauge's current value.

symbols.name: GaugeMetricValue

fields.name: Description
fields.doc:
Description is the instrument's human-readable docstring, or "" when
nobody described it. See SumMetricValue.Description.

fields.name: Points
fields.doc: Points holds the name's series, sorted by attribute set.

symbols.doc:
GaugeMetricValue is every series of ONE gauge instrument name.

It carries no Temporality, and that absence is the model, not an omission: a
gauge is a sampled reading, so there is no window for it to cover and OTLP's
Gauge message has no temporality field either. The one-field struct exists so
that all three kinds present the same walk to an exporter — an exporter that
had to special-case gauges would special-case them in every format.

symbols.name: GaugeValue

fields.name: Attrs
fields.doc:
Attrs is the series' attribute set, sorted by Key; nil for the
dimensionless series. See SumValue.Attrs for the aliasing rule.

fields.name: Value
fields.doc: Value is the last reading taken.

symbols.doc:
GaugeValue is one series of a gauge metric: the attribute set that identifies
it plus its instantaneous reading.

symbols.name: Histogram
symbols.doc: Histogram records a distribution of observations into fixed buckets.

symbols.name: Record
symbols.doc: Record observes one value, incrementing its bucket and the sum/count.

symbols.name: RecordDuration
symbols.doc: RecordDuration observes d as seconds (latency-histogram convenience).

symbols.name: HistogramMetricValue

fields.name: Temporality
fields.doc:
Temporality says which window Points cover. Never
TemporalityUnspecified.

fields.name: Description
fields.doc:
Description is the instrument's human-readable docstring, or "" when
nobody described it. See SumMetricValue.Description.

fields.name: Points
fields.doc: Points holds the name's series, sorted by attribute set.

symbols.doc:
HistogramMetricValue is every series of ONE histogram instrument name, plus
its temporality.

Exponential (base-2) histograms, which the OTel model also defines, are not
implemented: they are a different bucketing scheme with their own scale /
offset / zero-count fields, and adding them is a second point type rather
than a field on this one. Deferred by ADR 0044 §Deferred.

symbols.name: HistogramValue
symbols.spelled: struct{Attrs []coreotel.AttrValue; Bounds []float64; Counts []uint64; Sum float64; Count uint64}
symbols.canonical: struct{Attrs []github.com/kitsunium/sdk/internal/core/observe/otel.AttrValue; Bounds []float64; Counts []uint64; Sum float64; Count uint64}

fields.name: Attrs
fields.doc:
Attrs is the series' attribute set, sorted by Key; nil for the
dimensionless series. See SumValue.Attrs for the aliasing rule.

fields.name: Bounds
fields.doc:
Bounds holds the histogram's explicit upper bounds, ascending. OTLP
calls this field explicit_bounds.

fields.name: Counts
fields.doc:
Counts holds one count per bucket plus the +Inf overflow slot. The
counts are PER BUCKET, not cumulative — a format that wants a
cumulative ladder (Prometheus) builds it as it walks.

fields.name: Sum
fields.doc: Sum is the total of every observed value in the window.

fields.name: Count
fields.doc: Count is how many observations the window holds.

symbols.doc:
HistogramValue is one series of a histogram metric: the attribute set that
identifies it, the explicit bucket upper bounds, the count per bucket
(len == len(Bounds)+1, the last being the +Inf overflow), and the Sum/Count
of every observation in the window.

symbols.name: InstrumentKindConflict

code.public: That instrument name is already registered with a different kind

symbols.doc: InstrumentKindConflict is returned when a name is reused for a different kind.

symbols.name: Int64Callback
symbols.doc:
Int64Callback is read ONCE PER COLLECTION and reports the instrument's
current ABSOLUTE value — not a delta. That is the OTel contract for an
asynchronous sum: the callback states what the total is now
(runtime.NumGoroutine(), bytes allocated since boot), and the SDK differences
successive observations itself when the meter is a delta reader.

A callback MUST NOT call Collect on the meter that is collecting it, and MUST
NOT block: it runs inline in the collection, so a slow callback is a slow
scrape for every other instrument too.

symbols.name: InvalidAttribute

code.public: An attribute key is empty or repeated, or its value was never set

symbols.doc: InvalidAttribute is the panic sentinel for an unusable attribute set.

symbols.name: InvalidDescription

code.public: An instrument description must not be empty

symbols.doc: InvalidDescription is the panic sentinel for an empty Describe.

symbols.name: InvalidLabelName

code.public: An attribute key is not a valid Prometheus label name

symbols.doc:
InvalidLabelName is returned when an attribute key cannot be spelled as
a Prometheus label name.

symbols.name: InvalidMetricName

code.public: An instrument name is not a valid Prometheus metric name

symbols.doc:
InvalidMetricName is returned when an instrument name cannot be spelled
as a Prometheus metric name.

symbols.name: InvalidTemporality

code.public: That aggregation temporality is not one this SDK declares

symbols.doc:
InvalidTemporality is the panic sentinel for a Temporality that is none
of the three declared constants.

symbols.name: LookupExporter
symbols.doc:
LookupExporter returns the Exporter registered under name.

IFACE-PLUGIN: the registry stores plug-in exporters behind the Exporter
interface — concrete backend types stay unexported.

symbols.name: Meter
symbols.spelled: interface{Collect() SnapshotValue; Counter(name string, attrs ...coreotel.AttrValue) Counter; Gauge(name string, attrs ...coreotel.AttrValue) Gauge; Histogram(name string, buckets []float64, attrs ...coreotel.AttrValue) Histogram}
symbols.canonical: interface{Collect() github.com/kitsunium/sdk/internal/core/observe/metrics.SnapshotValue; Counter(name string, attrs ...github.com/kitsunium/sdk/internal/core/observe/otel.AttrValue) github.com/kitsunium/sdk/internal/core/observe/metrics.Counter; Gauge(name string, attrs ...github.com/kitsunium/sdk/internal/core/observe/otel.AttrValue) github.com/kitsunium/sdk/internal/core/observe/metrics.Gauge; Histogram(name string, buckets []float64, attrs ...github.com/kitsunium/sdk/internal/core/observe/otel.AttrValue) github.com/kitsunium/sdk/internal/core/observe/metrics.Histogram}
symbols.doc:
Meter mints named, attributed instruments and collects their values.

A SERIES is one instrument name plus one attribute set, and it is the unit of
identity: repeated calls with the same name and the same attributes return
the SAME instrument, so observations from every call site accumulate in one
place. Attribute ORDER is not part of the identity — the set is a set, and
{a,b} and {b,a} resolve to the same series. Passing no attributes at all is
legitimate and names the dimensionless series.

A name reused across instrument KINDS is a programmer error. So is an
attribute set with an empty key, a repeated key, or a value no constructor
ever set: all three are structure, fixed at the call site, and an
implementation is expected to refuse them loudly.

Implementations MUST be safe for concurrent use, and MUST bound how many
distinct attribute sets one name may hold — an unbounded attribute set is a
memory incident, not a reporting inconvenience.

This interface is FROZEN. `pkg/v1/observe/metrics.Meter` is a type alias to it, Go
interfaces are structural, and adding a method would break every downstream
implementer at compile time with no deprecation window (ADR 0039). The
instruments it lacks live on UpDownMeter and AsyncMeter, and FullMeter is the
union every in-tree constructor actually returns.

symbols.name: Collect
symbols.doc:
Collect returns a point-in-time SnapshotValue of every series.

Under TemporalityDelta it is a MUTATION: it consumes the window it
reports. Two independent collectors would then each receive half the
observations, so a delta meter has exactly one reader.

symbols.name: NormalizeResource
symbols.doc:
NormalizeResource returns the ResourceValue a Meter publishes: attributes
sorted, validated, owned, and carrying ServiceNameKey whether or not the
caller supplied it. An unusable attribute set panics with InvalidAttribute,
at construction, rather than at the first export.

symbols.name: NormalizeScope
symbols.doc:
NormalizeScope returns the ScopeValue a Meter publishes, filling an empty Name
with DefaultScopeName. Version is left exactly as supplied.

symbols.name: OTLPEndpointInvalid

code.public: The OTLP endpoint is not an absolute http or https URL with a path

symbols.doc:
OTLPEndpointInvalid is returned by NewOTLPHTTPExporter when the
configured endpoint cannot be a metrics collector URL.

symbols.name: OTLPExportRejected

code.public: The OTLP collector rejected the metrics payload

symbols.doc:
OTLPExportRejected is returned when a collector refuses the payload with
a status the specification marks non-retryable.

symbols.name: OTLPExportUnavailable

code.public: The OTLP collector is unreachable or overloaded

symbols.doc:
OTLPExportUnavailable is returned when an OTLP/HTTP export fails in a way
the specification says may be retried.

symbols.name: OTLPInvalidBucketLayout

code.public: That histogram's buckets have no OTLP representation

symbols.doc:
OTLPInvalidBucketLayout is returned when a histogram point's buckets
cannot be spelled as explicit_bounds plus bucket_counts.

symbols.name: OTLPPartialSuccess

code.public: The OTLP collector accepted the request but rejected some data points

symbols.doc:
OTLPPartialSuccess is returned when a collector accepts the request but
rejects some of its data points.

symbols.name: OTLPUnresolvedTemporality

code.public: That aggregation temporality has no OTLP representation

symbols.doc:
OTLPUnresolvedTemporality is returned when a snapshot's temporality has
no OTLP enum value.

symbols.name: ObserveFloat64
symbols.doc: ObserveFloat64 is ObserveInt64 for a double-valued observable.

symbols.name: ObserveInt64
symbols.doc:
ObserveInt64 reports ONE integer measurement, with its own attribute set,
from inside an Int64Callback. It is valid only for the duration of that call;
retaining it and calling it later observes into a collection that has already
finished.

It is a FUNC port, not a single-method interface, for the reason ADR 0041
gives: a published func type cannot grow a method, so it cannot break a
downstream implementer the way widening an interface would (ADR 0039).

symbols.name: OverflowAttrKey
symbols.doc:
OverflowAttrKey names the reserved attribute the meter attaches to the single
aggregated series it folds observations into once an instrument has reached
its cardinality bound. It is spelled with underscores rather than dots so it
needs no mangling to be a legal Prometheus label name — unlike every
OTel-conventional key, which is dotted.

The key is RESERVED: a caller who passes it explicitly with a BOOL value is
writing into the same series the meter uses for overflow, and their
observations merge with it. That is not enforced — enforcing it would cost a
comparison per attribute on the lookup path to prevent a collision nobody
reaches by accident.

symbols.name: RegisterExporter
symbols.doc:
RegisterExporter inserts e under e.Name() and returns it for singleton
binding. Panics on a nil exporter or a distinct exporter on a taken Name.

IFACE-PLUGIN: the registry hands plug-in Exporter instances back to callers so
each backend keeps its concrete type unexported.

"Nil" here means UNUSABLE, not only an untyped nil: a typed nil pointer and a
plug-in whose type is not comparable both satisfy the port and neither can
serve one call (see internal/kernel/plugin).

symbols.name: ReservedLabelName

code.public: An attribute key is reserved by the Prometheus exposition format

symbols.doc: ReservedLabelName is returned when an attribute key is legal but reserved.

symbols.name: SnapshotValue
symbols.spelled: struct{Resource coreotel.ResourceValue; Scope coreotel.ScopeValue; StartTime time.Time; Time time.Time; Sums map[string]SumMetricValue; Gauges map[string]GaugeMetricValue; Histograms map[string]HistogramMetricValue}
symbols.canonical: struct{Resource github.com/kitsunium/sdk/internal/core/observe/otel.ResourceValue; Scope github.com/kitsunium/sdk/internal/core/observe/otel.ScopeValue; StartTime time.Time; Time time.Time; Sums map[string]github.com/kitsunium/sdk/internal/core/observe/metrics.SumMetricValue; Gauges map[string]github.com/kitsunium/sdk/internal/core/observe/metrics.GaugeMetricValue; Histograms map[string]github.com/kitsunium/sdk/internal/core/observe/metrics.HistogramMetricValue}

fields.name: Resource
fields.doc: Resource identifies the producer, carried once for the whole payload.

fields.name: Scope
fields.doc:
Scope identifies the instrumentation, carried once for the whole
payload.

fields.name: StartTime
fields.doc:
StartTime opens the window every point covers. Under
TemporalityCumulative it is the meter's own start and repeats across
collections; under TemporalityDelta it advances to the previous
collection's Time.

It is one value for the whole snapshot rather than one per point
because every point in one Collect covers the same window. An encoder
that needs it per point (OTLP does) copies this one down.

fields.name: Time
fields.doc: Time closes the window: the instant the collection was taken.

fields.name: Sums
fields.doc:
Sums maps an instrument name to its sum metric — Counters and
UpDownCounters together, told apart by SumMetricValue.Monotonic.

fields.name: Gauges
fields.doc: Gauges maps an instrument name to its gauge metric.

fields.name: Histograms
fields.doc: Histograms maps an instrument name to its histogram metric.

symbols.doc:
SnapshotValue is a point-in-time copy of every series in a Meter, handed to
an Exporter. It is the OTel payload hierarchy flattened into one Go value:
Resource once, Scope once, then metrics keyed by name, each carrying its own
points — ResourceMetrics → ScopeMetrics → Metric → data points, with the two
single-element levels collapsed because one Meter has exactly one of each.

The shape is deliberately "instrument name -> its metric", not
"series key -> value": every wire format an exporter targets groups by name
first (Prometheus emits one TYPE header per name followed by its series; OTLP
nests data points inside one Metric). An exporter iterating these maps writes
its header once per key and its points from the slice, with no regrouping
pass and no composite key to re-parse.

Two properties an exporter may rely on:

  - Each Points slice is SORTED by attribute set, so a snapshot renders
    byte-identically twice in a row given the same values — which is what
    makes exporter output diffable and its tests writable without a sort of
    their own.
  - Each Attrs slice is sorted by Key and nil for the dimensionless series,
    so len(Attrs) == 0 is the "no braces" case rather than something to
    special-case per exporter.

symbols.name: SumMetricValue
symbols.spelled: struct{Temporality Temporality; Monotonic bool; Description string; Points []SumValue}
symbols.canonical: struct{Temporality github.com/kitsunium/sdk/internal/core/observe/metrics.Temporality; Monotonic bool; Description string; Points []github.com/kitsunium/sdk/internal/core/observe/metrics.SumValue}

fields.name: Temporality
fields.doc:
Temporality says which window Points cover. Never
TemporalityUnspecified — a Meter resolves it at construction.

fields.name: Monotonic
fields.doc:
Monotonic is true for a Counter and false for an UpDownCounter. A
backend uses it to decide whether a decrease is a reset or a reading.

fields.name: Description
fields.doc:
Description is the instrument's human-readable docstring, or "" when
nobody described it. It is NON-IDENTIFYING — the OTel data model says so
outright — so it never joins the series identity and an exporter that
cannot carry it loses nothing but the prose. See Describer.

fields.name: Points
fields.doc: Points holds the name's series, sorted by attribute set.

symbols.doc:
SumMetricValue is every series of ONE sum instrument name, plus the two facts
the OTel data model attaches to the metric rather than to its points.

A Counter and an UpDownCounter both produce a SumMetricValue; they differ
only by Monotonic. That is the model's own economy, and it is why the SDK has
two instrument interfaces and one point shape.

symbols.name: SumValue

fields.name: Attrs
fields.doc:
Attrs is the series' attribute set, sorted by Key; nil for the
dimensionless series.

The slice ALIASES the meter's own copy — it is not cloned per Collect.
The meter never mutates an attribute set after the series is created,
so a reader is safe; a writer would corrupt every future snapshot.
Cloning instead would cost one allocation per series per collection,
i.e. it would scale the cost of scraping with cardinality, which is
the exact axis the cardinality bound exists to contain.

fields.name: Value
fields.doc:
Value is the series' total: cumulative since the meter started, or the
delta since the previous collection, according to
SumMetricValue.Temporality.

symbols.doc:
SumValue is one series of a sum metric: the attribute set that identifies it
plus its value. Monotonicity and temporality are NOT here — they belong to
the metric, not to the point, which is the OTel data model's own split.

symbols.name: Temporality
symbols.doc:
Temporality says which time window a metric's reported value covers. It is
the single most load-bearing concept in the OpenTelemetry metrics data model,
because the same number means two different things under the two settings and
nothing in the number itself says which.

symbols.name: Resolved
symbols.doc:
Resolved maps the UNSET zero value onto the temporality a Meter actually
implements, and refuses anything that is neither of the three constants.

TemporalityUnspecified CLAMPS to TemporalityCumulative rather than refusing,
and the reason is not convention: an in-memory meter accumulates into atomics
and never resets them unless it is asked to, so "cumulative" is a DESCRIPTION
of what the unconfigured meter does, not a value invented on the caller's
behalf. Any other default would be a claim about the implementation that the
implementation does not honour (ADR 0031 §clamp).

An out-of-range value can only come from a deliberate cast — Temporality(7)
is not something a caller reaches by forgetting a field — so it is a
programming error and panics with InvalidTemporality rather than being
quietly folded into the default, which would hide the cast forever.

symbols.name: String
symbols.doc: String returns the spelling used in diagnostics and in the text exporter.

symbols.name: TemporalityCumulative
symbols.doc:
TemporalityCumulative means each point covers the window since the
series started: (T0,T1], then (T0,T2]. The reported number is a running
total and a reader differences successive collections itself.

symbols.name: TemporalityDelta
symbols.doc:
TemporalityDelta means each point covers the window since the previous
collection: (T1,T2], then (T2,T3]. The reported number is consumed by
the collection that reads it and starts again from zero.

symbols.name: TemporalityUnspecified
symbols.doc:
TemporalityUnspecified is the zero value and means "the caller has not
chosen". It is legal ONLY in a MeterConfig, where it resolves to
TemporalityCumulative; it never reaches a SnapshotValue.

symbols.name: UnknownExporter

code.public: No metrics exporter is registered under that name

symbols.doc: UnknownExporter is returned when no Exporter is registered under a Name.

symbols.name: UnsupportedTemporality

code.public: The Prometheus exposition format carries cumulative metrics only

symbols.doc:
UnsupportedTemporality is returned when a snapshot that is not
cumulative — delta, or an unresolved temporality — is handed to the
Prometheus exporter.

symbols.name: UpDownCounter
symbols.doc:
UpDownCounter is a NON-MONOTONIC sum: a running total that may go down as
well as up — in-flight requests, queue depth, open connections.

It is not a Gauge. A gauge is a sampled reading with no arithmetic behind it
("the temperature is 21.5"); an up-down counter is a total every call site
contributes to ("this handler took one slot, that one released it"), which is
why it is additive and a gauge is not. In the OTel data model both a Counter
and an UpDownCounter produce a Sum, and MONOTONICITY IS A FIELD OF THAT SUM
rather than a second point type — which is exactly why the two interfaces
exist at the API and only one shape exists in SumMetricValue.

It is a sibling of Counter rather than a widening of it, and structurally
distinct from it by Dec: a Counter is not silently usable where an
UpDownCounter is required.

symbols.name: Add
symbols.doc: Add adjusts the total by delta, which may be negative.

symbols.name: Dec
symbols.doc: Dec subtracts one.

symbols.name: Inc
symbols.doc: Inc adds one.

symbols.name: UpDownMeter
symbols.doc:
UpDownMeter mints the non-monotonic sum Meter cannot — the instrument for a
total that goes down as well as up.

A sibling interface rather than a fourth method on Meter, per ADR 0039: Meter
is published through a `pkg/v1` type alias, Go interfaces are structural, and
widening one breaks every downstream implementer at compile time.

symbols.name: ValidateAttrs
symbols.doc:
ValidateAttrs panics with InvalidAttribute (0.2.9.4) when sorted cannot name
a series: an empty Key, a value no constructor ever set, or the same Key
twice. It is the check every instrument fetch runs, on the already sorted
set; the rules are the shared model's (internal/core/observe/otel.ValidateAttrs), the
code is this signal's.

symbols.name: AttrKind
symbols.doc:
AttrKind discriminates the type of an AttrValue's value. It is the OpenTelemetry
attribute model: a value is a string, a bool, a signed 64-bit integer or a
double — never a string that happens to spell one of the others.

symbols.name: AttrKindBool
symbols.doc: AttrKindBool marks a bool-valued attribute.

symbols.name: AttrKindFloat64
symbols.doc: AttrKindFloat64 marks an IEEE-754 double attribute.

symbols.name: AttrKindInt64
symbols.doc: AttrKindInt64 marks a signed 64-bit integer attribute.

symbols.name: AttrKindInvalid
symbols.doc:
AttrKindInvalid is the zero value, and it names no type. An AttrValue
carrying it was built by a struct literal rather than by a
constructor, so its value was never set; every signal refuses it rather
than inventing an empty string for it (ADR 0031).

symbols.name: AttrKindString
symbols.doc: AttrKindString marks a string-valued attribute.

symbols.name: AttrValue

fields.name: Key
fields.doc:
Key names the dimension. It must be non-empty and appear at most once
in an attribute set; ValidateAttrs checks both.

symbols.doc:
AttrValue is one dimension — of a metric series, of a span, of a Resource: a
Key naming the dimension and a TYPED value observed for it.

The Key is STRUCTURE and the value is DATA. A key is written at the call site
and is constant for the lifetime of the process ("http.request.method"); a
value comes from whatever the process is measuring and varies per observation
("GET", 503, true). That asymmetry is why an unusable key is a programmer
error the signal panics on, while an unbounded stream of values is a runtime
condition — the meter absorbs it into an overflow series.

The value is unexported and reachable only through Kind and the four typed
accessors, so the only way to build a usable AttrValue is one of the four
constructors — String, Bool, Int64, Float64. A struct literal can still set
Key, and the resulting AttrKindInvalid is refused rather than silently read
as an empty string.

symbols.name: AppendIdentity
symbols.doc:
AppendIdentity appends an INJECTIVE binary encoding of the attribute's value
— its kind tag followed by fixed-width or length-prefixed bytes — to dst.

The kind tag is what keeps String("v", "1") and Int64("v", 1) apart: without
it the two would encode identically and two series carrying different
dimensions would silently accumulate into one. It lives with the type rather
than in the meter so that every Meter implementation inherits the same
injectivity instead of re-deriving it.

symbols.name: AppendText
symbols.doc:
AppendText appends the canonical TEXT rendering of the attribute's value.

Only AttrKindString can produce a byte an exposition format would have to
escape: a bool renders as "true"/"false", and an integer or a double renders
through strconv, so all three are drawn from [0-9a-zA-Z+-.] alone. An
exporter can therefore escape the string case and append the other three
verbatim.

symbols.name: Bool
symbols.doc: Bool returns the bool value, and false for every other kind.

symbols.name: Float64
symbols.doc: Float64 returns the double value, and zero for every other kind.

symbols.name: Int64
symbols.doc: Int64 returns the integer value, and zero for every other kind.

symbols.name: Kind
symbols.doc: Kind reports which type the attribute's value has.

symbols.name: Str
symbols.doc: Str returns the string value, and the empty string for every other kind.

symbols.name: Bool
symbols.doc: Bool returns a bool-valued AttrValue.

symbols.name: CompareAttrKey
symbols.doc:
CompareAttrKey orders two attributes by Key alone. A package-level function
value, not a closure, so passing it to slices.SortFunc allocates nothing.

symbols.name: CompareAttrValue
symbols.doc:
CompareAttrValue orders two attribute VALUES totally: kind first, then the
value within the kind. It never allocates.

The ordering distinguishes exactly the pairs AppendIdentity distinguishes,
which is what a Collect-time sort needs: if two values that name two
different series compared equal, their relative order would depend on the map
iteration that produced them and a snapshot would stop rendering identically
twice in a row. That is why a double falls back to its BIT PATTERN when the
numeric comparison ties — +0.0 and -0.0, and two NaNs with different
payloads, are distinct series and must be distinct here too.

symbols.name: Float64
symbols.doc:
Float64 returns a double AttrValue.

A float is a poor dimension — it is a measurement, not a category — and the
identity encoding keys it on its IEEE-754 BIT PATTERN, so -0.0 and +0.0 name
two different series and two NaNs with different payloads name two more. The
kind exists because the OTel attribute model has it and an OTLP payload can
carry it, not because a metric wants it.

symbols.name: Int64
symbols.doc: Int64 returns a signed-integer AttrValue.

symbols.name: NormalizeResource
symbols.doc:
NormalizeResource returns the ResourceValue a Meter or a Tracer publishes:
attributes sorted, validated, owned, and carrying ServiceNameKey whether or
not the caller supplied it. An unusable attribute set panics with refusal's
message, at construction, rather than at the first export.

The service.name default is not an SDK invention — the OpenTelemetry
specification mandates unknown_service for exactly this case, so the clamp
substitutes nobody's judgement (ADR 0031 §clamp).

It is a function and not a method because refusal is the CALLER'S: a method
on the shared type would have to pick one signal's code for both.

symbols.name: NormalizeScope
symbols.doc:
NormalizeScope returns scope with an empty Name filled by defaultName.
Version is left exactly as supplied.

The default is a PARAMETER because it is the one part of the shared model
that must not be shared: a scope names the library that produced THIS
signal, so a span batch stamped with the metrics package's name would tell a
backend that the metrics package emitted spans. Each signal passes its own
DefaultScopeName (ADR 0051 §Decision 2).

symbols.name: ResourceValue

fields.name: Attrs
fields.doc:
Attrs are the producer's attributes, sorted by Key. A ResourceValue
normalised by NormalizeResource always carries ServiceNameKey.

symbols.doc:
ResourceValue identifies the ENTITY that produced the telemetry — the
service, the process, the host. Its attributes are carried ONCE per payload
rather than on every point or span, which is the whole reason the concept
exists: service.name on ten thousand data points is ten thousand copies of
one fact.

SchemaURL is deliberately absent. It is optional in the specification, this
SDK emits no semantic-convention version, and a field that is always empty is
a placeholder (CLAUDE.md rule 5). It lands the day the SDK pins a convention
version, next to Attrs, and nothing else about the shape changes.

symbols.name: ScopeValue

fields.name: Name
fields.doc:
Name is the instrumenting library's name. Empty means unset and
resolves to the signal's own default — see NormalizeScope.

fields.name: Version
fields.doc:
Version is the instrumenting library's version. It is optional in the
specification and stays empty when the caller has none — inventing one
would be a claim about code this package cannot see.

symbols.doc:
ScopeValue identifies the INSTRUMENTATION that produced the telemetry — the
library, package or module that minted the instruments or started the spans,
as opposed to the service that runs it. OpenTelemetry calls it
InstrumentationScope, and it is what lets a backend tell "the SDK's own http
metrics" apart from "the application's".

SchemaURL and scope-level attributes are absent for the reason
ResourceValue's SchemaURL is: both are optional in the specification, nothing
in this SDK produces either, and an always-empty field is a placeholder.

symbols.name: ServiceNameKey
symbols.doc:
ServiceNameKey is the attribute key OpenTelemetry's resource semantic
conventions reserve for the logical name of the service. It is dotted, like
every OTel-conventional key — which is exactly why the Prometheus connector
cannot carry it (see internal/service/observe/metrics/CLAUDE.md §What the Prometheus
connector loses). It is also the key a backend correlates a trace with a
metric on, which is why both signals read it from here.

symbols.name: SortAttrs
symbols.doc:
SortAttrs returns a sorted, validated, owned copy of attrs — the cold-path
form of what the meter does with a stack buffer on every fetch, and what a
Resource, a span, an event and a link do once each. It panics with refusal's
message on an unusable set, for the reason ValidateAttrs gives.

symbols.name: String
symbols.doc:
String returns a string-valued AttrValue. It is the shortest of the four to write
because a string dimension is the overwhelmingly common one.

symbols.name: UnknownService
symbols.doc:
UnknownService is the value the OpenTelemetry specification mandates when a
producer supplies no service.name. The spec allows appending the executable
name to it; this SDK does not, because a binary path is not a service
identity and would silently become one on a dashboard.

symbols.name: ValidateAttrs
symbols.doc:
ValidateAttrs panics with refusal's message when sorted cannot name a
dimension set: an empty Key, a value no constructor ever set, or the same Key
twice.

It runs on the ALREADY SORTED set so duplicates are adjacent and the check
costs one comparison per attribute. Panicking is safe for the reason the
meter's cross-kind name refusal is: an attribute key and an attribute KIND
are both structure, written at the call site, so they are wrong on the first
call or never. The alternative is a set no exporter can emit — Prometheus and
OTLP both reject an empty attribute name — failing far away, inside the
component the SDK told the caller to stop thinking about.

refusal is the CALLER'S sentinel — an *errs.Error in every caller this SDK
has, typed here as the error it is so the model needs no import of its own:
the signal whose API was misused names the defect with its own dotted-quad
code, and this package owns none. It is read only to panic.

symbols.name: CaptureCanceled

code.public: The profile was abandoned before its window ended

symbols.doc:
CaptureCanceled is a CPU capture whose context ended before the window
did. The profiler is stopped and nothing is returned: a partial window
would read as the whole one. The context's error is joined.

symbols.name: CaptureFailed

code.public: The profile could not be written

symbols.doc:
CaptureFailed wraps an error runtime/pprof returned while writing a
profile: the heap, or the goroutines.

symbols.name: CodeCaptureCanceled
symbols.doc:
CodeCaptureCanceled identifies a CPU capture whose context ended before its
window.

symbols.name: CodeCaptureFailed
symbols.doc: CodeCaptureFailed identifies a profile the runtime could not write.

symbols.name: CodeProfileMalformed
symbols.doc:
CodeProfileMalformed identifies bytes that are not a well-formed pprof
profile.

symbols.name: CodeProfileTooLarge
symbols.doc:
CodeProfileTooLarge identifies a profile over the engine's MaxProfileBytes,
compressed or decompressed, or whose stacks resolve to more than its
MaxFrames frames.

symbols.name: CodeProfilerBusy
symbols.doc:
CodeProfilerBusy identifies a CPU capture refused because the process's one
CPU profiler is already running.

symbols.name: CodeSampleTypeMissing
symbols.doc:
CodeSampleTypeMissing identifies a fold asked for a sample type the profile
does not measure.

symbols.name: CodeWindowInvalid
symbols.doc:
CodeWindowInvalid identifies a CPU capture window that is not positive or
exceeds the engine's MaxCPUWindow.

symbols.name: FlameNodeValue

fields.name: Name
fields.doc: Name is the function's name; [FlameRoot] for the root.

fields.name: Children
fields.doc: Children are the functions it called, costliest first.

fields.name: Value
fields.doc: Value is the cost of every sample through this path.

symbols.doc:
FlameNodeValue is one frame of a flame graph: a function reached along one
path, and what the samples through it cost.

symbols.name: FlameRoot
symbols.doc:
FlameRoot is the name of a flame graph's root frame, which stands for the
whole profile.

symbols.name: FoldedValue
symbols.spelled: struct{Flame *FlameNodeValue; Owners []OwnerCostValue; Top []FunctionCostValue; SampleType SampleTypeValue; Total int64; Unattributed int64}
symbols.canonical: struct{Flame *github.com/kitsunium/sdk/internal/core/observe/profiling.FlameNodeValue; Owners []github.com/kitsunium/sdk/internal/core/observe/profiling.OwnerCostValue; Top []github.com/kitsunium/sdk/internal/core/observe/profiling.FunctionCostValue; SampleType github.com/kitsunium/sdk/internal/core/observe/profiling.SampleTypeValue; Total int64; Unattributed int64}

fields.name: Flame
fields.doc:
Flame is the flame graph, rooted at [FlameRoot], its children the
outermost frames; nil when Total is zero.

fields.name: Owners
fields.doc: Owners holds each owner's cost, the costliest first.

fields.name: Top
fields.doc:
Top holds the costliest functions: by flat cost, then cumulative, then
name.

fields.name: SampleType
fields.doc: SampleType is what was folded.

fields.name: Total
fields.doc: Total is the sum of every sample's value.

fields.name: Unattributed
fields.doc:
Unattributed is the part of Total charged to nobody. Total is exactly
Unattributed plus every owner's Value.

symbols.doc:
FoldedValue is a profile folded: in the sample type's own unit —
nanoseconds of CPU, bytes of heap — never rounded.

symbols.name: FrameValue
symbols.spelled: struct{Function string; File string; Line int; StartLine int; Address uint64}
symbols.canonical: struct{Function string; File string; Line int; StartLine int; Address uint64}

fields.name: Function
fields.doc:
Function is the function's name as the runtime spells it —
"pkg.(*T).Method", "pkg.F.func1", "pkg.G[...]" — or empty for a frame
no symbol was found for.

fields.name: File
fields.doc: File is the function's source file, as recorded when it was compiled.

fields.name: Line
fields.doc: Line is the line executing in this frame; zero when unknown.

fields.name: StartLine
fields.doc:
StartLine is the line the function starts at; zero when unknown, and
always zero in a goroutine dump, which does not print it.

fields.name: Address
fields.doc:
Address is the program counter of an unsymbolized frame; zero
otherwise.

symbols.doc:
FrameValue is one frame of a stack: a function, where it is defined, and
the line executing in it.

symbols.name: FunctionCostValue
symbols.spelled: struct{Function string; File string; Flat int64; Cum int64; StartLine int}
symbols.canonical: struct{Function string; File string; Flat int64; Cum int64; StartLine int}

fields.name: Function
fields.doc: Function is the function's name, as the runtime spells it.

fields.name: File
fields.doc: File and StartLine say where it is defined, when the profile knows.

fields.name: Flat
fields.doc: Flat is the cost of samples whose innermost frame is the function.

fields.name: Cum
fields.doc:
Cum is the cost of samples with the function anywhere on the stack,
each sample counted once however many times the function recurses.

fields.name: StartLine
fields.doc: StartLine is the function's first line; zero when unknown.

symbols.doc:
FunctionCostValue is what one function cost, flat and cumulative, and where
it is defined.

symbols.name: GoroutineGroupValue
symbols.spelled: struct{Labels map[string]string; State string; Top string; Stack []FrameValue; Count int}
symbols.canonical: struct{Labels map[string]string; State string; Top string; Stack []github.com/kitsunium/sdk/internal/core/observe/profiling.FrameValue; Count int}

fields.name: Labels
fields.doc:
Labels holds the grouping labels the goroutines carry, by key; a key
they do not carry is absent.

fields.name: State
fields.doc: State is the goroutines' state.

fields.name: Top
fields.doc:
Top is the innermost frame that is not the runtime's own machinery —
the code that asked to wait — or the innermost frame when every frame
is the runtime's.

fields.name: Stack
fields.doc: Stack is one member's stack, innermost first.

fields.name: Count
fields.doc: Count is how many goroutines share the group.

symbols.doc:
GoroutineGroupValue is goroutines sharing their labels, their state and
their top frame.

symbols.name: GoroutineValue
symbols.spelled: struct{Labels map[string]string; CreatedBy FrameValue; State string; Stack []FrameValue; Waiting time.Duration; ID int64; Creator int64; LockedToThread bool}
symbols.canonical: struct{Labels map[string]string; CreatedBy github.com/kitsunium/sdk/internal/core/observe/profiling.FrameValue; State string; Stack []github.com/kitsunium/sdk/internal/core/observe/profiling.FrameValue; Waiting time.Duration; ID int64; Creator int64; LockedToThread bool}

fields.name: Labels
fields.doc: Labels are the goroutine's pprof labels.

fields.name: CreatedBy
fields.doc:
CreatedBy is the frame of the go statement that started the goroutine;
zero for the main goroutine and for those the runtime starts itself.

fields.name: State
fields.doc:
State is the runtime's word for what the goroutine does: "running",
"runnable", "syscall", or what it waits on — "select", "chan receive",
"IO wait", "sleep", "sync.Mutex.Lock".

fields.name: Stack
fields.doc: Stack is the goroutine's stack, innermost frame first.

fields.name: Waiting
fields.doc:
Waiting is how long the goroutine has been blocked, to the minute the
runtime reports; zero under a minute or when it is not blocked.

fields.name: ID
fields.doc: ID is the goroutine's number.

fields.name: Creator
fields.doc:
Creator is the number of the goroutine that ran the go statement; zero
when the dump does not say.

fields.name: LockedToThread
fields.doc: LockedToThread says the goroutine is locked to its OS thread.

symbols.doc:
GoroutineValue is one goroutine of the process, as the runtime's dump
describes it.

symbols.name: OwnerCostValue

fields.name: Owner
fields.doc: Owner is the name Attribute returned.

fields.name: Top
fields.doc: Top holds the owner's costliest functions.

fields.name: Value
fields.doc: Value is the sum of the samples charged to the owner.

symbols.doc:
OwnerCostValue is what one owner cost: the sum of the samples charged to
it, and its own costliest functions.

symbols.name: ProfileMalformed

code.public: That is not a well-formed pprof profile

symbols.doc:
ProfileMalformed refuses bytes that are not a well-formed pprof
profile: a truncated field, a wire type a field cannot have, an index
into the string, function or location table that points nowhere, a
sample whose values do not match the sample types, a gzip stream that
does not inflate. The field says which part; the input is never quoted.

symbols.name: ProfileTooLarge

code.public: The profile is too large to read

symbols.doc:
ProfileTooLarge refuses a profile over MaxProfileBytes, before reading
it or once it inflates past the bound, and one whose stacks resolve to
more than MaxFrames frames.

symbols.name: ProfileValue
symbols.spelled: struct{Time time.Time; SampleTypes []SampleTypeValue; Samples []SampleValue; Comments []string; PeriodType SampleTypeValue; DefaultSampleType string; Duration time.Duration; Period int64}
symbols.canonical: struct{Time time.Time; SampleTypes []github.com/kitsunium/sdk/internal/core/observe/profiling.SampleTypeValue; Samples []github.com/kitsunium/sdk/internal/core/observe/profiling.SampleValue; Comments []string; PeriodType github.com/kitsunium/sdk/internal/core/observe/profiling.SampleTypeValue; DefaultSampleType string; Duration time.Duration; Period int64}

fields.name: Time
fields.doc:
Time is when the collection started; zero when the profile does not
say.

fields.name: SampleTypes
fields.doc:
SampleTypes names what each of a sample's values measures, in order:
{cpu nanoseconds}, {inuse_space bytes}.

fields.name: Samples
fields.doc: Samples are the measured stacks.

fields.name: Comments
fields.doc: Comments are the profile's free-text comments.

fields.name: PeriodType
fields.doc:
PeriodType and Period say how often a sample is taken: every Period
PeriodType — 10 000 000 nanoseconds of CPU, 524 288 bytes allocated.

fields.name: DefaultSampleType
fields.doc:
DefaultSampleType is the sample type a viewer shows first; empty when
the profile does not say, and the last sample type is the convention.

fields.name: Duration
fields.doc: Duration is how long the collection lasted; zero when not recorded.

fields.name: Period
fields.doc: Period is the sampling period, in PeriodType's unit.

symbols.doc:
ProfileValue is a decoded pprof profile: what was measured, and every
sample with its stack, its values and its labels. It is plain data — the
profile.proto message with its tables resolved — and safe to share once
built.

symbols.name: ProfilerBusy

code.public: A CPU profile is already being recorded

symbols.doc:
ProfilerBusy refuses a CPU capture while the process's one CPU profiler
is running — started by another capture, or by anyone's
pprof.StartCPUProfile. It is not queued: the caller decides whether to
wait.

symbols.name: SampleTypeMissing

code.public: The profile does not measure that

symbols.doc:
SampleTypeMissing refuses a fold asked for a sample type the profile
does not measure — "cpu" of a heap profile.

symbols.name: SampleTypeValue

fields.name: Type
fields.doc: Type is what is measured: "cpu", "samples", "inuse_space".

fields.name: Unit
fields.doc: Unit is its unit: "nanoseconds", "count", "bytes".

symbols.doc:
SampleTypeValue names what a value measures and its unit — {cpu
nanoseconds}, {inuse_space bytes}.

symbols.name: SampleValue
symbols.spelled: struct{Labels map[string][]string; NumLabels map[string][]int64; Stack []FrameValue; Values []int64}
symbols.canonical: struct{Labels map[string][]string; NumLabels map[string][]int64; Stack []github.com/kitsunium/sdk/internal/core/observe/profiling.FrameValue; Values []int64}

fields.name: Labels
fields.doc:
Labels are the pprof labels of the goroutine, by key: set with
pprof.Do or pprof.SetGoroutineLabels. A CPU profile carries them; a
heap profile does not.

fields.name: NumLabels
fields.doc:
NumLabels are the numeric labels, by key — a heap sample's "bytes",
the size of each object it counts.

fields.name: Stack
fields.doc:
Stack is the sample's call stack, innermost frame first. A call the
compiler inlined is a frame of its own, before the frame it was
inlined into.

fields.name: Values
fields.doc: Values holds one value per ProfileValue.SampleTypes entry.

symbols.doc:
SampleValue is one sample: a stack, a value per sample type, and the labels
the goroutine carried when it was taken.

symbols.name: WindowInvalid

code.public: A CPU profile needs a window longer than zero and at most five minutes

symbols.doc:
WindowInvalid refuses a CPU window that is not positive — a profile
of no time is empty by construction — or that exceeds MaxCPUWindow.

symbols.name: AvailableExporters
symbols.doc: AvailableExporters returns the sorted list of registered ExporterNames.

symbols.name: BatchExporterMissing

code.public: The batch span sink needs an exporter

symbols.doc: BatchExporterMissing is returned by NewBatchSink when no usable exporter is configured.

symbols.name: BatchFlushIncomplete

code.public: The batch span sink did not finish exporting before the deadline

symbols.doc: BatchFlushIncomplete reports a ForceFlush or Shutdown cut short by its context.

symbols.name: Carrier
symbols.spelled: interface{Get(key string) string; Set(key string, value string)}
symbols.canonical: interface{Get(key string) string; Set(key string, value string)}
symbols.doc:
Carrier is the two-method surface a header set has to present for a span
context to travel through it.

It is exactly http.Header's Get/Set pair, on purpose and to the letter, so
the engine's `trace.Inject(ctx, req.Header)` compiles with no adapter — and
so this package still imports no net/http, which would drag an HTTP opinion
into a contract that also has to serve a message queue and a gRPC metadata
map.

IFACE-PLUGIN: it is FROZEN at two methods (ADR 0039). Adding a third — Del,
Values, a multi-value read — would break every downstream two-method double at
compile time with no deprecation window, and every one of those additions is
reachable as a sibling interface instead. Two is also what makes http.Header
satisfy it structurally, which is the whole ergonomics.

symbols.name: CodeBatchExporterMissing
symbols.doc:
CodeBatchExporterMissing identifies a batch sink built with no exporter, or
with one that cannot serve a call: a batch with nowhere to go has no safe
default (ADR 0031).

symbols.name: CodeBatchFlushIncomplete
symbols.doc:
CodeBatchFlushIncomplete identifies a ForceFlush or Shutdown whose context
ended before every queued span had been handed to the exporter.

symbols.name: CodeDuplicateRegistration
symbols.doc:
CodeDuplicateRegistration identifies a boot-time SpanExporter registry
collision: a nil exporter, or a distinct exporter claiming a taken Name.

symbols.name: CodeEntropyFailed
symbols.doc:
CodeEntropyFailed identified a crypto/rand.Read failure while drawing the
bytes of a trace or span identifier. Nothing returns it since Go 1.24,
whose crypto/rand.Read cannot fail; the code stays allocated and published.

symbols.name: CodeExportFailed
symbols.doc:
CodeExportFailed identifies a span exporter that returned an error while
shipping a batch (the exporter's cause rides the wrap trail).

symbols.name: CodeInvalidAttribute
symbols.doc:
CodeInvalidAttribute identifies an attribute set a span, an event, a link or
a Resource cannot carry: an attribute with an empty Key, the same Key twice,
or a value no constructor ever set (AttrKindInvalid). The rules are the
shared model's (internal/core/observe/otel); this code is the trace signal's own,
where it used to borrow the metrics one (0.2.9.4) because the model lived in
internal/core/observe/metrics.

symbols.name: CodeInvalidSampleRatio
symbols.doc:
CodeInvalidSampleRatio identifies a Ratio sampler asked for a fraction that
is not one: NaN, negative, above 1, or exactly 0 — which is NeverSample under
a name that also spells "unconfigured" (ADR 0031).

symbols.name: CodeInvalidSpanName
symbols.doc:
CodeInvalidSpanName identifies a Start call with an empty span name. A span's
name is the low-cardinality operation label every backend groups on, so an
empty one produces a trace nobody can search for.

symbols.name: CodeInvalidTraceParent
symbols.doc:
CodeInvalidTraceParent identifies a traceparent header that cannot be read as
a span context: a malformed field, the invalid version "ff", or an all-zero
trace-id or parent-id — the two values W3C Trace Context declares invalid.

symbols.name: CodeInvalidTraceState
symbols.doc:
CodeInvalidTraceState identifies a tracestate header that does not match the
W3C list grammar: a key or value outside its character set, more than 32 list
members, or the same key twice.

symbols.name: CodeOTLPEndpointInvalid
symbols.doc:
CodeOTLPEndpointInvalid identifies an OTLP/HTTP exporter configured with an
endpoint that is not an absolute http(s) URL carrying a path — the address
the POST would otherwise be sent to blind.

symbols.name: CodeOTLPExportRejected
symbols.doc:
CodeOTLPExportRejected identifies a collector that refused the payload
PERMANENTLY: an HTTP status outside the specification's retryable set, so
replaying the same bytes would fail the same way.

symbols.name: CodeOTLPExportUnavailable
symbols.doc:
CodeOTLPExportUnavailable identifies a TRANSIENT OTLP/HTTP failure — a
transport fault, or one of the four statuses the specification lists as
retryable. The same bytes may succeed later.

symbols.name: CodeOTLPInvalidSpanContext
symbols.doc:
CodeOTLPInvalidSpanContext identifies a span handed to the OTLP/JSON encoder
whose trace-id or span-id is all zeroes. Both are declared invalid by W3C
Trace Context and required by the schema, so there is no honest hex to emit.

symbols.name: CodeOTLPPartialSuccess
symbols.doc:
CodeOTLPPartialSuccess identifies a collector that accepted the request
(HTTP 200) but rejected some of its spans. The specification forbids retrying
it, so the loss is reported rather than replayed.

symbols.name: CodeOTLPSpanNotEnded
symbols.doc:
CodeOTLPSpanNotEnded identifies a span handed to the OTLP/JSON encoder with no
EndTime. `end_time_unix_nano` is required, and a zero would claim the span
ended at the Unix epoch.

symbols.name: CodeUnknownExporter
symbols.doc:
CodeUnknownExporter identifies an Export/Lookup naming a span exporter that no
imported package has registered.

symbols.name: ContextSpanExporter
symbols.spelled: interface{ExportContext(ctx context.Context, spans SpansValue) error; SpanExporter}
symbols.doc:
ContextSpanExporter is a SpanExporter whose export can be bounded and
cancelled: ExportContext ships spans under ctx, and returns once ctx is done
at the latest. The OpenTelemetry SDK specification says an export MUST NOT
block indefinitely; Export has no context to bound it with, and SpanExporter
is a published port, so the bound arrives as this sibling rather than as a
widened method (ADR 0039). A caller holding a SpanExporter asks for it with a
type assertion, as ExportContext and the batch sink do.

Implementations MUST be safe for concurrent use, and Export keeps its
meaning: it is ExportContext under a context the exporter bounds itself.

symbols.name: ContextWithSpan
symbols.doc:
ContextWithSpan returns a copy of parent carrying span's context, exactly as
ContextWithSpanContext(parent, span.SpanContext()) would — SpanContextFromContext
reads the same value back — without copying that value onto the heap.

The context stores the span itself and asks it for its context when the
context is read. A span the tracer returns is a pointer, so storing it costs
no allocation, where boxing the span context does: an unsampled Start pays
two allocations instead of three. The price is the contract it states: span's
SpanContext must return the same value for as long as the context lives,
which every span Start returns guarantees — its identity is immutable once
minted. A nil span reads back as the invalid zero context, and shadows any
outer one as ContextWithSpanContext's invalid context does.

symbols.name: ContextWithSpanContext
symbols.doc:
ContextWithSpanContext returns a copy of parent carrying context.

An INVALID context is still stored rather than skipped. Storing it is what
makes "this scope deliberately has no trace" expressible: a handler that ran
under an unsampled or absent traceparent shadows any outer context instead of
silently re-parenting its children onto it.

symbols.name: DefaultExportTimeout
symbols.doc:
DefaultExportTimeout bounds one export when the caller's context carries no
deadline of its own: 30 s, the OpenTelemetry trace SDK specification's default
for a batch processor's exportTimeout (OTEL_BSP_EXPORT_TIMEOUT). The
specification says an export MUST NOT block indefinitely, and a context with
no deadline is how an indefinite block is written; a caller who wants another
bound puts it on the context.

symbols.name: DefaultScopeName
symbols.doc:
DefaultScopeName names this SDK's TRACE package as the instrumenting library
when a caller declares no scope of their own.

It is a separate constant from metrics' DefaultScopeName, and the difference is
not cosmetic: an InstrumentationScope names the library that produced THIS
signal, so stamping a span batch with `…/pkg/v1/observe/metrics` would tell a backend
that the metrics package emitted spans. Sharing the value would have been the
one place where sharing the model stopped being reuse and started being a
wrong answer — which is exactly the line ADR 0051 §Decision 2 draws, and why
internal/core/observe/otel takes the default as a parameter rather than owning one.

symbols.name: DocumentExporter
symbols.doc:
DocumentExporter is the sibling of ContextSpanExporter an exporter
implements when it can ship a batch already encoded as its wire
document: ExportDocument sends doc under ctx, as ExportContext sends
the spans it would have encoded into it, with the same verdicts.
The OTLP/HTTP exporter implements it, doc being an OTLP/JSON
ExportTraceServiceRequest — what EncodeOTLPJSON writes —, so a
batch encoded and stored by a store-and-forward queue is posted
later without being decoded (ADR 0185). An empty doc sends nothing.

A caller holding a ContextSpanExporter asks for it with a type
assertion (ADR 0039). Implementations MUST be safe for concurrent use.

symbols.name: DuplicateRegistration

code.public: A trace exporter is already registered under that name

symbols.doc: DuplicateRegistration is the boot-time SpanExporter-registry panic sentinel.

symbols.name: EntropyFailed

code.public: Trace identifier generation failed to read secure random bytes

symbols.doc:
EntropyFailed was the wrap of a crypto/rand.Read failure while drawing
trace or span id bytes. Nothing returns it since Go 1.24, whose
crypto/rand.Read never fails; it stays published with its value.

symbols.name: EventValue

fields.name: Time
fields.doc:
Time is when it happened. An unset instant encodes as 0, which is what
the schema means by an unknown timestamp.

fields.name: Name
fields.doc: Name is the event's low-cardinality label.

fields.name: Attrs
fields.doc: Attrs are the event's typed dimensions, sorted by Key.

symbols.doc:
EventValue is one thing that happened at an instant during a span, rather than
over an interval — `opentelemetry/proto/trace/v1.Span.Event`.

An event is not a cheap child span, and the distinction is worth stating
because the wrong choice is invisible until a trace is unreadable: an event
has no identity, no duration and no children, so nothing can be a child of it
and nothing can link to it. Use one for a moment worth marking on a span's
timeline (a retry, a cache miss, an exception); use a child span for work that
took time.

symbols.name: Normalized
symbols.doc:
Normalized returns the event a span actually records: attributes sorted,
validated and owned, so the caller's slice cannot be mutated afterwards
through the span.

symbols.name: ExceptionEventName
symbols.doc: ExceptionEventName is the reserved event name for a recorded error.

symbols.name: ExceptionMessageKey
symbols.doc: ExceptionMessageKey names the error's message.

symbols.name: ExceptionStacktraceKey
symbols.doc:
ExceptionStacktraceKey names the error's stack trace. This SDK never
fills it: a Go error carries no stack, and inventing one from the
recording site would name the wrong goroutine.

symbols.name: ExceptionTypeKey
symbols.doc: ExceptionTypeKey names the error's type.

symbols.name: Export
symbols.doc:
Export ships spans through the SpanExporter registered as name. A missing
exporter returns UnknownExporter; an exporter failure wraps as ExportFailed.

symbols.name: ExportContext
symbols.spelled: func(ctx context.Context, name ExporterName, spans SpansValue) error
symbols.doc:
ExportContext ships spans through the SpanExporter registered as name, bounded
by ctx. A missing exporter returns UnknownExporter; an exporter failure wraps
as ExportFailed.

When ctx carries no deadline, DefaultExportTimeout is applied: the
specification forbids an export that blocks indefinitely. An exporter that
implements ContextSpanExporter receives the bounded context through
ExportContext; one that implements only SpanExporter is called through Export,
which has no context to honour, and is bounded by nothing but itself — every
exporter that touches a network in this SDK implements the sibling.

symbols.name: ExportFailed

code.public: The trace exporter failed to ship the spans

symbols.doc: ExportFailed wraps an exporter's failure while shipping spans.

symbols.name: ExporterName
symbols.doc:
ExporterName is the typed key under which a SpanExporter registers (e.g.
"otlpjson"). The zero value ExporterName("") is reserved invalid.

The registry is deliberately the same shape as core/observe/metrics' — the same
kernel/plugin.Registry underneath, named, reached by blank-importing the
exporter's package, config-addressable. It EARNS its
keep here for the reason it earns it there and for one more: ADR 0051
§Decision 5 requires the OTLP/HTTP emitter to be absent from it, and "absent
from the registry" is only a statement anyone can check if there is a registry
to be absent from. A test pins that absence.

symbols.name: String
symbols.doc: String returns the raw name.

symbols.name: FlagSampled
symbols.doc:
FlagSampled is the sampled bit: the least significant one. When set, the
caller "may have recorded trace data" (§3.2.2.5.1), which is what makes the
sampling decision a property of the TRACE rather than of each span.

symbols.name: InvalidAttribute

code.public: An attribute key is empty or repeated, or its value was never set

symbols.doc:
InvalidAttribute is the panic sentinel for an unusable attribute set on
a span, an event, a link or a Resource.

symbols.name: InvalidSampleRatio

code.public: A sampling ratio must be greater than 0 and at most 1

symbols.doc:
InvalidSampleRatio is returned when Ratio is handed a fraction it will
not turn into a sampler.

symbols.name: InvalidSpanName

code.public: A span name must not be empty

symbols.doc: InvalidSpanName is the panic sentinel for a Start call with no name.

symbols.name: InvalidTraceParent

code.public: The traceparent header is not a valid W3C trace context

symbols.doc:
InvalidTraceParent is returned when a traceparent header cannot be read.
Its Public never echoes the header: it is attacker-controlled text.

symbols.name: InvalidTraceState

code.public: The tracestate header is not a valid W3C trace state list

symbols.doc: InvalidTraceState is returned when a tracestate header cannot be read.

symbols.name: LinkValue

fields.name: Context
fields.doc:
Context identifies the linked span. A link whose context is invalid is
dropped rather than emitted — it names nothing.

fields.name: Attrs
fields.doc: Attrs describe the relationship, sorted by Key.

symbols.doc:
LinkValue points at a span that is causally related to this one but is not its
parent — `opentelemetry/proto/trace/v1.Span.Link`.

The canonical case is a batch: one consumer span processes fifty messages
produced by fifty different traces. Making any one of them the parent would be
a lie about forty-nine, and making the batch a child of all fifty is not a
tree. A link says "related, elsewhere" without claiming ancestry.

It carries a whole SpanContextValue rather than a loose trace-id/span-id pair
because the linked context's tracestate and sampled bit are part of what a
backend needs: a link into a trace that was never sampled points at spans
nobody stored.

symbols.name: IsValid
symbols.doc: IsValid reports whether the link names a joinable span.

symbols.name: Normalized
symbols.doc:
Normalized returns the link a span actually records: attributes sorted,
validated and owned.

symbols.name: LookupExporter
symbols.doc:
LookupExporter returns the SpanExporter registered under name.

IFACE-PLUGIN: the registry stores plug-in exporters behind the SpanExporter
interface — concrete backend types stay unexported.

symbols.name: MaxTraceStateKeyLen
symbols.doc:
MaxTraceStateKeyLen is the longest legal key: `simple-key = lcalpha
0*255(...)` is 1 + 255 characters.

symbols.name: MaxTraceStateMembers
symbols.doc:
MaxTraceStateMembers is the list cap: `list = list-member 0*31( OWS ","
OWS list-member )` is 32 members, no more.

symbols.name: MaxTraceStateValueLen
symbols.doc:
MaxTraceStateValueLen is the longest legal value: `value = 0*255(chr)
nblk-chr` is 255 + 1 characters.

symbols.name: NewStateBuilder
symbols.doc:
NewStateBuilder returns an empty builder with room for size members. A size
above MaxTraceStateMembers is clamped to it — no list holds more — and a
negative one is read as zero.

symbols.name: NormalizeResource
symbols.doc:
NormalizeResource returns the ResourceValue a Tracer publishes: attributes
sorted, validated, owned, and carrying ServiceNameKey whether or not the
caller supplied it. An unusable attribute set panics with InvalidAttribute,
at construction, rather than at the first export.

symbols.name: NormalizeScope
symbols.doc:
NormalizeScope returns the ScopeValue a Tracer publishes, filling an empty Name
with DefaultScopeName. Version is left exactly as supplied: it is optional in
the specification, and inventing one would be a claim about code this package
cannot see.

symbols.name: OTLPEndpointInvalid

code.public: The OTLP endpoint must be an absolute http(s) URL with a path

symbols.doc: OTLPEndpointInvalid is returned when an OTLP/HTTP endpoint is unusable.

symbols.name: OTLPExportRejected

code.public: The trace collector rejected the export

symbols.doc: OTLPExportRejected reports a permanent refusal by the collector.

symbols.name: OTLPExportUnavailable

code.public: The trace collector is unavailable

symbols.doc: OTLPExportUnavailable reports a transient failure worth retrying.

symbols.name: OTLPInvalidSpanContext

code.public: A span carries an all-zero trace or span identifier

symbols.doc: OTLPInvalidSpanContext is returned when a span carries an unusable id.

symbols.name: OTLPPartialSuccess

code.public: The trace collector accepted the request but rejected some spans

symbols.doc: OTLPPartialSuccess reports an accepted request with rejected spans.

symbols.name: OTLPSpanNotEnded

code.public: A span reached the exporter without an end time

symbols.doc: OTLPSpanNotEnded is returned when a span reaches the encoder unended.

symbols.name: ParseSpanID
symbols.doc:
ParseSpanID reads 16 lowercase hex digits into a SpanID, refusing an all-zero
result for the reason ParseTraceID does.

symbols.name: ParseTraceID
symbols.doc:
ParseTraceID reads 32 lowercase hex digits into a TraceID, refusing an
all-zero result.

Uppercase is refused rather than folded: the traceparent grammar is 32HEXDIGLC
and a producer emitting uppercase is producing a header other vendors will
reject, so accepting it here would hide the defect exactly one hop from where
it was introduced.

symbols.name: RegisterExporter
symbols.doc:
RegisterExporter inserts e under e.Name() and returns it for singleton
binding. Panics on a nil exporter or a distinct exporter on a taken Name.

IFACE-PLUGIN: the registry hands plug-in SpanExporter instances back to
callers so each backend keeps its concrete type unexported.

"Nil" here means UNUSABLE, not only an untyped nil: a typed nil pointer and a
plug-in whose type is not comparable both satisfy the port and neither can
serve one call (see internal/kernel/plugin).

symbols.name: Sampler
symbols.doc:
Sampler decides whether a span is recorded and exported. It reports true to
keep the span, false to drop it.

It is a FUNC port, not an interface, applying ADR 0041 structurally: a
published func type cannot grow a method at all, so there is no widening to
forbid and no sibling to invent later.

# The decision is taken ONCE, at the root

This is the load-bearing rule of the whole domain and it is not a convention —
it is what the `sampled` bit of traceparent is FOR. A Tracer consults a
Sampler only when it is starting a root span; every child, in this process or
in any process downstream, inherits the answer through
SpanContextValue.IsSampled.

Deciding per span produces a trace with holes in the middle, and a trace with
holes is worse than no trace: a span whose parent was dropped becomes an
orphan a backend renders as its own root, so one request appears as several
unrelated ones and the latency of the whole is unrecoverable. The failure is
also invisible at the point that causes it — the process that dropped the
parent shows nothing wrong at all.

A Sampler is therefore consulted on ROOT spans only. That is a property of the
Tracer, stated here because this is where a reader will look for it.

# Concurrency

A Sampler MUST be safe for concurrent use and MUST NOT block: it runs inline
on the goroutine starting the span, before any work the span measures.
