On Unix its permission bits answer "who could have created this entry".
On Windows os.Stat synthesises the bits from one read-only attribute, so
they answer nothing there and a caller needing that answer must get it
from the platform's own access-control model. This package reports what
it read and takes no position on what it means.

fields.name: Mode
fields.doc:
Mode is the mode of the component itself, as lstat reports it: an
indirection is described here, never traversed to describe its target.

fields.name: Info
fields.doc:
Info is the whole of that lstat answer — Mode is Info.Mode() — for what
a mode does not say. On Unix, Info.Sys() is the *syscall.Stat_t naming
the component's OWNER, which is how a policy tells a component this
account or root created from one another account did. It is read the
way Container is, relative to the handle of the directory the component
was found in, never by a second lookup of Path; and like Mode it
describes an indirection itself, never its target.

fields.name: Target
fields.doc:
Target is where the indirection points, exactly as the filesystem stores
it — relative or absolute, unresolved. It is empty unless Indirect.

fields.name: Indirect
fields.doc:
Indirect records that this component is a symbolic link on Unix or a
reparse point on Windows, so resolving the path CONTINUED somewhere the
component's own name does not say.

symbols.doc:
StepValue describes one component of a resolved path: what that component
IS, and who could have put it there.

The second half is the reason this type exists. Knowing that a component is
a symbolic link answers almost nothing on its own, because the answer is
"yes" for /tmp on macOS, for /var/run on most Linux distributions, and for
C:\Users\All Users on Windows — all of them legitimate, all of them planted
by the operating system's installer. What separates those from an attack is
not the link, it is the DIRECTORY THE LINK LIVES IN: a link in a directory
only root can write was put there by root, and a link in a world-writable
directory was put there by anybody at all.

So every step carries Container, the mode of the directory the component was
looked up in, read by fstat on a handle this package held open rather than
by a second path lookup that could resolve somewhere else.

symbols.name: ContentRights
symbols.doc:
ContentRights is what lets its holder alter or remove a FILE created in
the directory, read off the entries such a file inherits: write or
append its data, delete it, or rewrite its list. It is asked through
onFilesWithin.

symbols.name: CreateRights
symbols.doc:
CreateRights is what lets its holder put a DIRECTORY at a name nobody has
taken. A path component is always a directory — a junction and a
directory symbolic link are both created with FILE_ADD_SUBDIRECTORY, and
a file cannot be a component of a longer path — so this is the question
to ask of the directory HOLDING a component.

symbols.name: GrantsAnyone
symbols.spelled: func(dir string, onDirectory uint32, onFilesWithin uint32) (granted bool, observed string)
symbols.canonical: func(dir string, onDirectory uint32, onFilesWithin uint32) (granted bool, observed string)
symbols.doc:
GrantsAnyone reports whether dir's DACL grants a right in onDirectory to an
identifier meaning anybody — Everyone, Authenticated Users, BUILTIN\Users —
or a right in onFilesWithin through the entries the files created in dir
inherit. A zero mask asks nothing of its half.

Every discretionary ACE shape is decoded, denials are subtracted in list
order and per modelled account, and a NULL DACL is read as the full grant it
is; an EMPTY one, the opposite, grants nobody anything and falls out of the
walk as no grant. observed names the grant found ("S-1-1-0=0x40"), or — with
granted false — what kept a verdict from being reached: the Win32 status
("GetNamedSecurityInfoW=5"), a path that is not one
("UTF16PtrFromString=…"), or the entry the walk could not fetch
("GetAce#3"). It is EMPTY only when the list was read to the end and grants
nothing asked about. What a caller does with "no verdict" is the caller's
decision — the reader takes none.

symbols.name: ReplaceRights
symbols.doc:
ReplaceRights is what lets its holder take away an entry it did not
create — the Windows spelling of the Unix rule that refuses 0777 and
accepts 0777|sticky. RightAddFile is deliberately not in it: creating an
entry at a free name is exactly what the sticky bit permits.

symbols.name: RightAddFile
symbols.doc:
RightAddFile is FILE_ADD_FILE: create a file at a free name. On a file
the same bit is FILE_WRITE_DATA.

symbols.name: RightAddSubdirectory
symbols.doc:
RightAddSubdirectory is FILE_ADD_SUBDIRECTORY: create a directory — or a
junction — at a free name. On a file the same bit is FILE_APPEND_DATA.

symbols.name: RightDelete
symbols.doc:
RightDelete is DELETE, the standard right that removes the object it is
held on — a FILE, when it is asked of what files inherit, rather than an
entry of the directory.

symbols.name: RightDeleteChild
symbols.doc:
RightDeleteChild is FILE_DELETE_CHILD: unlink an entry of this directory
WITHOUT owning it — the one right that turns an entry somebody created
into an entry somebody else may replace.

symbols.name: RightWriteDAC
symbols.doc:
RightWriteDAC is WRITE_DAC: rewrite the list, and so grant itself the
rest.

symbols.name: RightWriteOwner
symbols.doc: RightWriteOwner is WRITE_OWNER: take ownership, and so rewrite the list.

symbols.name: Registry
symbols.doc:
Registry is a process-wide table of plug-ins keyed by name: written at import
time, read on every dispatch. A reader loads an immutable snapshot and takes
no lock; a writer copies the table, inserts, and publishes the copy under the
snapshot's writer lock, so a reader never observes a half-built map and two
writers never lose each other's entry.

It decides nothing a domain names. Publish REPORTS whether the name was
already held by a different value — the conflict — and the registrar refuses
it with its own dotted-quad code and reason, exactly as it does with
Unusable's answer. Re-publishing the SAME value is an idempotent no-op that
reports no conflict, which is what lets a plug-in package be imported through
two paths without turning a diamond dependency into a boot panic. Claim
reports the holder instead of a verdict, for a registrar that refuses every
second registration or names the holder in its refusal.

V must be comparable, and that is a runtime contract as much as a compile
one: when V is an interface, == on a dynamic value that is not comparable
panics inside Publish's duplicate check with Go's message rather than the
registrar's. A registrar asks Unusable first, which refuses exactly that
value, and a typed nil with it.

The zero value is ready to use. K is ordered so Names can answer in a stable
order rather than in map order.

symbols.name: Claim
symbols.spelled: func(name K, value V) (holder V, taken bool)
symbols.canonical: func(name K, value V) (holder V, taken bool)
symbols.doc:
Claim inserts (name -> value) when name is free. When name is taken, nothing
changes and Claim reports the value holding it — value itself or another.

Publish is Claim plus the verdict most registrars want. Claim serves the two
that want another one: a registrar for which ANY second registration is a
conflict, the identical value included, refuses on taken alone; and a
registrar whose refusal names the holder reads it here, from the same atomic
step that refused, rather than from a second Lookup.

The check and the insert are one atomic step.

symbols.name: Lookup
symbols.doc:
Lookup returns the value registered under name, and whether there is one. A
miss returns V's zero value, so a caller checking only the value of an
interface-typed V would hold a nil — which is why found exists.

symbols.name: Names
symbols.doc:
Names returns every registered name in ascending order, or nil before the
first Publish or Claim. The slice is the caller's; it shares nothing with the
table.

symbols.name: Publish
symbols.doc:
Publish inserts (name -> value) and reports whether name was already held by
a DIFFERENT value. On a conflict nothing changes: the first registration
stays, and the caller refuses the second with its own code. Re-publishing the
identical value changes nothing either, and is not a conflict.

The duplicate check and the publish are one atomic step: Publish is Claim
with the verdict a registry that tolerates a diamond import wants.

symbols.name: Unusable
symbols.doc:
Unusable reports why v cannot be published into a registry, or the empty
string when it can. The reason is a fragment meant to follow a colon in the
caller's own message, e.g. "nil *gzip.compressor".

It is deliberately not a predicate returning bool: a registrar that refuses
must say which of the two shapes it refused, because "nil Compressor" and
"Compressor is not comparable" are found by different searches and fixed in
different places.

The parameter is a type PARAMETER rather than an `any`, which costs the
caller nothing — every registrar passes its port and T is inferred — and
keeps the signature from claiming to accept anything in particular. What is
judged is the dynamic value either way: reflect sees through the boxing.

symbols.name: Compare
symbols.doc:
Compare returns -1, 0 or +1 as v orders before, equal to or after w under
SemVer precedence. Build metadata is ignored, so v1.0.0+a and v1.0.0+b
compare equal.

An invalid string orders below every valid version and equal to every
other invalid string, so Compare is a total order over all strings and
slices.SortFunc(list, Compare) puts the unreadable ones first.

symbols.name: IsPseudoVersion
symbols.doc:
IsPseudoVersion reports whether v is a Go pseudo-version: a valid version
whose pre-release ends in "yyyymmddhhmmss-REVISION", immediately preceded
either by nothing, when the version is vX.0.0, or by an identifier "0" —
the three shapes of the Go modules reference, with or without build
metadata such as "+incompatible".

It recognises the SHAPE, as the toolchain's own pattern does: a stamp whose
fourteen digits are not a real instant still makes a pseudo-version, and
[PseudoVersionTime] is what reports that the time does not read.

symbols.name: IsValid
symbols.doc:
IsValid reports whether v is a version: SemVer 2.0.0 with a leading "v",
or one of the shorthands "vMAJOR" and "vMAJOR.MINOR".

symbols.name: Prerelease
symbols.doc:
Prerelease returns the pre-release part of v with its leading hyphen —
"-rc.1" for "v1.0.0-rc.1+build" — or "" when v has none: a release, a
shorthand, or a string that is not a version, which [IsValid] tells apart.

symbols.name: PseudoVersionRev
symbols.doc:
PseudoVersionRev returns the revision a pseudo-version names — by the
toolchain's convention a commit's first twelve hexadecimal digits — and
reports whether v is a pseudo-version at all. The revision is returned as
written: the grammar admits any ASCII letters and digits.

symbols.name: PseudoVersionTime
symbols.doc:
PseudoVersionTime returns the commit time a pseudo-version carries, in UTC
and to the second, and reports whether it could be read: false when v is
not a pseudo-version, or when its fourteen digits are not a real instant —
a thirteenth month, say — which [IsPseudoVersion] does not judge.

symbols.name: IndexByte2
symbols.spelled: func(b []byte, c1 byte, c2 byte) int
symbols.canonical: func(b []byte, c1 byte, c2 byte) int
symbols.doc:
IndexByte2 returns the index of the first byte of b equal to c1 or to c2,
or -1 when there is none: the search for a line end, '\r' or '\n'. A slice of 64 bytes or more goes to two scans of bytes.IndexByte
where the build has no AVX2 form.

symbols.name: IndexLess
symbols.doc:
IndexLess returns the index of the first byte of b below n, or -1 when
there is none. A bound of zero holds no byte. The search is a word at a
time for a bound of 128 or less, and byte by byte above it.

symbols.name: NewSet
symbols.spelled: func(first byte, second byte, below byte, upper bool) Set
symbols.canonical: func(first byte, second byte, below byte, upper bool) github.com/kitsunium/sdk/internal/kernel/swar.Set
symbols.doc:
NewSet returns the set of the bytes first and second, the bytes below
below, and — when upper is true — the bytes from 0x80 up. Pass the same
byte twice for a set of one, and a below of zero for none below.

A below above 128 is accepted; [Set.Index] then reads byte by byte.

symbols.name: Set
symbols.doc:
Set is a set of byte values: the two bytes it was built with, the bytes
below its bound, and optionally the bytes from 0x80 up. [NewSet] computes
what a search reads once, and [Set.Index] only reads it, so a Set is safe
for any number of goroutines. The zero Set holds the byte 0x00 alone.

symbols.name: Index
symbols.doc:
Index returns the index of the first byte of b that is in the set, or -1
when there is none. It reads nothing past len(b).

symbols.name: Config

fields.name: Output
fields.doc:
Output is where a command's OWN output goes. It reaches a [corecli.Action] as
InvocationValue.Output, so a command never has to reach for a process
stream itself.

The zero value resolves to os.Stderr, NOT os.Stdout. ADR 0030 makes
stdout a protocol channel that no SDK default may claim: a tool whose
output is a JSON document on a pipe sets Output: os.Stdout in main,
which is one visible line at the one place that can honestly make the
choice. A zero value is what somebody who has not yet learned the
question exists chose, so it must not be the dangerous one.

fields.name: ErrOutput
fields.doc:
ErrOutput is where the generated help, and the usage that follows a bad
command line, are written. The zero value resolves to os.Stderr.

It is a SECOND writer rather than the same one so that setting Output to
os.Stdout for a machine-readable tool does not put a help page in the
middle of the document a consumer is parsing.

What is deliberately NOT written here is the error itself. The engine
owns the help — it is generated from the declarations and only the SDK
can render it — and the caller owns how an error is presented, because a
caller may want it as a line on stderr, as a log record, or as JSON. Two
voices printing one failure is how a CLI ends up saying it twice.

symbols.doc:
Config configures one [New]. Its zero value is a working configuration.

It carries two writers and nothing else. There is no Signals field, no
shutdown budget, no logger, no config source and no env prefix: every one of
those is a domain the SDK already ships, and a CLI that grew its own copy
would be a second, weaker one that the first would eventually disagree with.
ADR 0065 §D6 lists what this domain composes and what it refuses to redo.

Config is a published concrete shape (pkg/v1/app/cli.Config aliases it), so ADR
0040 applies: it may still change while the module is v0, said out loud, and
not after v1.

symbols.name: FlagSource
symbols.doc:
FlagSource snapshots the flags an operator ACTUALLY TYPED on one invocation
and returns them as a configuration layer.

# Only what was set

It walks flag.FlagSet.Visit and never VisitAll. That one word is the whole
value of this adapter: VisitAll yields every DECLARED flag, including the
ones nobody passed, carrying their Go defaults — so a flag with a zero
default would override the file and the environment on every single run, and
a configuration file would appear to be ignored for reasons nothing reports.
Visit yields only what the command line actually carried, which is exactly
what "the flags are the highest-precedence layer" is supposed to mean.

# The flag name IS the config key

No transformation: no camelCase to snake_case, no "-" to "_", no automatic
prefixing. Every such rule is a second grammar a reader has to learn and a
generator has to reproduce, and its failure mode is a key nobody typed
silently not matching a field. A flag that feeds `database.max_conns`
declares itself as "database.max_conns" — package flag accepts a dot in a
name and parses -database.max_conns=5 without help. And when the name is
wrong, the config schema (ADR 0061) REFUSES an unaddressed key rather than
ignoring it, so the mistake is loud at startup.

# What this is not

It is not a configuration loader. It reads no file, no environment variable
and no default; it does no layering, no decoding and no validation. Those
are the config domain, they already exist, and a CLI carrying its own copy
would be a second one to disagree with. The intended shape is one line:

	err := config.LoadSchema(&cfg, schema,
		config.FileSource("toml", "/etc/tool.toml"),
		config.EnvSource("TOOL_"),
		cli.FlagSource(invocation)) // last wins

# Precedence inside one invocation

The sets are visited root first, so a leaf flag overrides an ancestor flag
of the same name — the same "later wins" direction config.Load already uses
between sources, rather than a second rule to remember.

symbols.name: FlagSourceValue
symbols.doc:
FlagSourceValue is one invocation's flags, shaped as the flat key→value
layer internal/core/app/config.Source yields. It is the whole of what this
domain contributes to configuration, and everything it deliberately is not
is listed in [FlagSource].

FlagSourceValue is a published concrete shape (pkg/v1/app/cli.FlagSource returns
it), so ADR 0040 applies: it may still change while the module is v0, said
out loud, and not after v1.

symbols.name: Load
symbols.doc: Load returns the layer. It satisfies internal/core/app/config.Source.

symbols.name: New
symbols.spelled: func(cfg Config, root corecli.CommandValue) (runner corecli.Executor, err error)
symbols.doc:
New validates a command tree and returns the [corecli.Executor] that runs it.

The WHOLE tree is validated here, not the branch an invocation happens to
take. A declaration is a wiring fact, and a wiring fault discovered by the
operator who typed the one command nobody had tried is a fault discovered in
production: `tool db migrate` being unreachable must fail on the first run
of the binary, not on the first run of the migration.

Every refusal is one of internal/core/app/cli's sentinels and carries EX_CONFIG
(78). A [corecli.Binder] is CALLED here, once, on a throwaway set — that is
what proves it binds no reserved name — so a Binder must be safe to call
more than once. A Binder that panics is deliberately not recovered: it runs
inside the caller's own main, on the line that wrote it, and a recovered
panic there would replace a stack pointing at the bug with a sentence about
a tree.

symbols.name: EnvSource
symbols.doc:
EnvSource returns a Source reading "PREFIX_KEY=value" env vars, stripping the
prefix and lower-casing the key. An EMPTY prefix — and only an empty prefix —
reads every variable.

The separating underscore is supplied by the Source, and a trailing one on
prefix is absorbed rather than doubled: EnvSource("APP") and EnvSource("APP_")
name the same namespace. Both spellings are natural to write, and the second
used to build the prefix "APP__", which matches nothing — Load then returned
an empty configuration and a nil error, so a typo cost the caller the whole
config with no signal at all.

That absorption can never empty a non-empty prefix. "" is not "a namespace
whose name is empty", it is the whole environment, so a prefix made only of
underscores names the "_" namespace instead of collapsing onto it.

symbols.name: FSSource
symbols.spelled: func(fsys fs.FS, format codec.Format, path string) coreconfig.Source
symbols.doc:
FSSource returns a Source reading path inside fsys and parsing it as format
(the codec must be registered — blank-import its package, e.g.
pkg/v1/data/codec). It is [FileSource] over an fs.FS: the same codec dispatch,
the same CONFIG_SOURCE_FAILED for every way the file cannot be read or
parsed, and the same description — layer "file", detail the path as given —
so a traced load reports it as a file. The reason it exists is a program
that carries its configuration inside its own binary:

	//go:embed config
	var files embed.FS

	source := config.FSSource(files, "yaml", "config/config.yaml")

path is an io/fs name — slash-separated and unrooted, fs.ValidPath — and a
name that is not one is refused when the source loads, before the
filesystem is asked: an fs.ReadFileFS receives the name as given, and one
that resolved "../x" would otherwise read outside the tree.

A file the filesystem does not hold is REFUSED, exactly as FileSource
refuses a path it cannot open, and never read as an empty layer. The two are
one source over two filesystems and must answer alike; and the usual reason
a file is missing from an embedded tree is a build mistake — an embed
pattern that matched nothing, a file renamed and not re-embedded — which,
read as empty, starts the program on its defaults with nothing said. A layer
that is optional by design is the caller's decision, one fs.Stat away.

A nil fsys is refused when the source loads, rather than panicking there.

symbols.name: FileSource
symbols.doc:
FileSource returns a Source reading path and parsing it as format (the codec
must be registered — blank-import its package, e.g. pkg/v1/data/codec).

symbols.name: Load
symbols.doc:
Load merges every source (later overrides earlier) into target, then runs
target.Validate() when target implements core/app/config.Validator. A source read
failure, a decode failure, or a validation failure abort with the matching
typed sentinel.

It declares no schema: no key is required, no default is applied, and a key
no field of T addresses is DROPPED by the decode exactly as encoding/json
drops it. That is a legitimate way to load a configuration — there is nothing
to contradict — and it is why the schema arrived as a second entry point
rather than as a widened signature nobody could opt out of. A caller who
wants the typo caught declares a schema and calls [LoadSchema].

A key is matched to a field the way encoding/json matches it, so "Port"
and "PORT" fill a field tagged "port": every layer is rewritten to the
spelling T declares before the merge, and later wins whatever case each
layer wrote. The keys of a map are data and keep their case, and two
fields whose names differ only by case are told apart by the exact
spelling, as the decoder tells them apart.

symbols.name: LoadSchema
symbols.doc:
LoadSchema is [Load] with a compiled [SchemaValue]: the schema's typed
defaults are merged UNDER every source, its required keys and its vocabulary
are checked against the merged map, and its constraints run over the decoded
result before the target's own Validate.

# The layer order, which is the whole contract

	default  <  file  <  env  <  any later source

The default layer is placed first STRUCTURALLY, not by argument order: there
is no way to spell a load in which a default outranks a source, because a
default that could win is not a default. Everything after it is the caller's
order, so an explicit override is simply the last Source — the port is one
method, and the SDK does not need a special type for "the values I decided
at the call site".

# An absent key and a key set to zero are different statements

Defaults are a LAYER merged before the decode, so presence is decided while
the operator's key still exists as a key. `timeout = 0` in a file is a key
that was supplied and stays 0; an omitted `timeout` is a key that was not,
and takes the default. A post-decode "if the field is zero, apply the
default" cannot tell those apart, and would silently overrule the operator
on every field whose zero value is meaningful — which is most of them.

A partially-supplied table keeps its unmentioned defaults: the merge folds
key-by-key, so a file setting `database.host` does not erase a default for
`database.max_conns`.

# The key pass runs first, and it runs once

A required key no source supplied fails HERE, at start-up, before anything
reads the value — that is the entire reason a schema exists. Every missing
key is named in one error, together with every key the target type cannot
address, so one restart tells an operator the whole truth.

The key pass is not merged into the value report that follows it. A key
nobody supplied decodes to a zero the operator never wrote, and running the
bounds on that zero would report a rule nobody violated — burying the one
fact that matters under a fact derived from it. The report is not truncated;
the second pass is simply not run over input already known to be fiction.

# What a failure says

A violation is reported at the OPERATOR's key ("database.max_conns"), never
at the Go field name, because the decode goes through a json round trip and
the json tag is literally the key they typed. The error carries the count,
the first rule and the offending keys; it carries no message and no value,
because a configuration value may be a password, a token or a connection
string. SchemaValue.Check returns the full report when messages are wanted.

A nil schema is refused by name rather than silently loading nothing.

symbols.name: LoadSchemaWithOrigins
symbols.spelled: func[T any](target *T, schema *SchemaValue[T], sources ...coreconfig.Source) (origins []coreconfig.OriginValue, err error)
symbols.canonical: func[T any](target *T, schema *github.com/kitsunium/sdk/internal/service/app/config.SchemaValue[T], sources ...github.com/kitsunium/sdk/internal/core/app/config.Source) (origins []github.com/kitsunium/sdk/internal/core/app/config.OriginValue, err error)
symbols.doc:
LoadSchemaWithOrigins is [LoadSchema] with the origins [LoadWithOrigins]
reports; a key the schema's defaults supplied is reported as "default". A
nil schema is refused by name, as LoadSchema refuses it.

symbols.name: LoadWithOrigins
symbols.doc:
LoadWithOrigins is [Load], and it also reports where every key of T got its
final value: one core/app/config.OriginValue per leaf key of T, sorted by key.

An origin names the LAYER — "default", "file", "env", or the kind a source
reports through core/app/config.Describer, else "source" with the source's
position — and the DETAIL an operator acts on: the variable that set the
key ("APP_DATA_DIR"), the file that holds it. It never carries the value,
and a key whose field holds a core/security/secret.Value is marked Secret, so a
--show-config rendering knows to mask whatever it prints beside it. A key
absent from the merged layers — no layer supplied it, or a later one erased
it by replacing one of its tables with a scalar or a null — is reported with
an empty Layer: its field holds its zero.

The load itself is exactly [Load]'s — same order, same verdicts — and on a
failure no origin is returned: a configuration that did not load has no
provenance worth reading.

symbols.name: NewSchemaValue
symbols.doc:
NewSchemaValue compiles spec into a [SchemaValue], refusing at CONSTRUCTION every
declaration that could not work — which is the whole point of having one.

Refused with CONFIG_SCHEMA_INVALID, each naming the key and the clause:

  - a key outside the grammar (empty, an empty segment, a leading or
    trailing separator);
  - a key that names no field of T — a typo in a declared key would
    otherwise produce a default that silently never applies, or a
    requirement that can never be satisfied, which are the two quietest ways
    a configuration can be wrong;
  - the same key declared twice, or declared both as a value and as a table;
  - a key declared both REQUIRED and with a default, in either order and at
    either nesting level. The schema would fill the key itself, so the
    requirement could never fire, and a clause that cannot fire is read as
    protection;
  - a default the loader's JSON round trip cannot carry, or that does not
    decode into the field it targets ("eighty" for an int port);
  - a default that violates the constraint the schema itself declares for
    that key. That is ADR 0031's exact trap: a schema whose default sits
    outside its own bounds produces an invalid configuration on precisely
    the deployment where nobody set the key, and reports it as the
    OPERATOR's fault.

A tag the validation domain refuses surfaces THAT domain's error unchanged
(INVALID_RULE / CONSTRAINT_MISCONFIGURED), not a config code: its fields
already name the field, the rule and the clause, and relabelling would throw
away the diagnosis to gain a code the caller has to look up anyway.

A T with no `validate` tag, no Required and no Default is a valid, accepting
schema — which still refuses an unknown key.

symbols.name: PollWatcher
symbols.doc:
PollWatcher returns a Watcher that polls path every interval and invokes the
onChange callback when the file's mtime or size changes.

symbols.name: SchemaSpec
symbols.spelled: [T any] struct{Required []string; Defaults []coreconfig.DeclaredValue; AllowUnknownKeys bool; Rule corevalidation.Constraint[T]}
symbols.canonical: [T any] struct{Required []string; Defaults []github.com/kitsunium/sdk/internal/core/app/config.DeclaredValue; AllowUnknownKeys bool; Rule github.com/kitsunium/sdk/internal/core/app/validation.Constraint[T]}

fields.name: Required
fields.doc:
Required names the keys a load must find in some source. A key listed
here and absent from every layer fails the LOAD — at start-up, before
anything reads the value — and every missing key is named in one error
rather than the first one found.

It is a KEY-level statement, decided on the merged map while the key is
still a key. That is what distinguishes it from the validation domain's
`required` tag, which is a VALUE-level statement decided after the
decode, where an absent key and an explicit zero are the same bytes.
`port = 0` written in a file satisfies this and fails `validate:"required"`;
declare both when both are meant.

A required key may not also carry a default: see Defaults.

fields.name: Defaults
fields.doc:
Defaults are the typed values keys take when NO Source supplied them.
Each is checked at construction against the type, against the grammar,
and against the constraints the schema itself declares for that key.

A key here may not also appear in Required — nor may either be nested
under the other. A required key the schema itself fills can never be
missing, so the requirement would be a clause that cannot fire, and a
clause that cannot fire is worse than no clause: it is read as
protection. The contradiction is refused at construction (ADR 0031).

fields.name: AllowUnknownKeys
fields.doc:
AllowUnknownKeys stops the load refusing a key no field of T addresses.

The zero value REFUSES, and that is the whole point: a schema is the
statement "these are the keys I read", so a key outside it is either a
typo or a deliberate extra. Ignoring it silently is the classic
production incident — `APP_PORTT=9090` decodes into nothing, the process
starts on the old port, and the only evidence is the absence of an
effect.

Set it when the source genuinely carries more than this type reads: a
configuration file shared by two services, or an unprefixed EnvSource,
which hands over every variable in the process environment. Those are
facts about the SOURCE, and the opt-out is where the author says so.

A key that differs from one of T's only by case is not unknown: the
decoder fills that field from it, and the load rewrites it to T's
spelling before the check.

fields.name: Rule
fields.doc:
Rule is one extra constraint, composed with the `validate` tags of T
into a single report. It is where a CROSS-FIELD rule lives — "a TLS
certificate without its key", "a replica count above the node count" —
because a per-field tag has no vocabulary for a second field and
inventing one is how a tag dialect turns into a language (ADR 0046).

It is deliberately singular. The validation domain already ships the
combinator (validation.All), so a slice here would be a second spelling
of composition that the reader has to learn — and the one that cannot
express "all of these, but stop at the first" the way the real
combinators can. Pass validation.All(a, b) for several.

A rule reports at core/app/validation.RootPath when no single key is at
fault, which is exactly what the grammar reserves the root for.

symbols.doc:
SchemaSpec declares a configuration's SHAPE: which keys the application
reads, which of them it cannot start without, what each holds when nobody
supplies it, and what the decoded result must satisfy.

The zero value is a legitimate declaration. It requires nothing, defaults
nothing, and adds no rule of its own — but the `validate` struct tags of T
still apply, because a schema that ignored the tags on the very type it
describes would be a second place to look for the same answer, and it still
refuses an unknown key, because that is the check the zero value must not
silently disarm. A configuration with nothing declared passes, which is
ADR 0031's accepting half: "nothing is declared" and "something is declared
wrongly" are opposite states and only the second is a defect.

symbols.name: SchemaValue
symbols.doc:
SchemaValue is a compiled configuration shape: the default LAYER it
contributes, the keys it requires, the vocabulary it accepts, and the
constraint the decoded configuration must satisfy. Build one with
[NewSchemaValue]; the zero value is not usable and [LoadSchema] refuses a nil one
by name rather than loading nothing and reporting success.

It is safe for concurrent use and is meant to be built once, at start-up,
and kept. pkg/v1/app/config.Schema aliases it.

symbols.name: Check
symbols.doc:
Check runs the schema's VALUE constraints against an already-decoded value
and returns the FULL located report — every violation, at the operator's key.

It answers only the value question. The KEY questions — was a required key
supplied, did a source carry a key nothing reads — are not answerable from a
decoded T at all: after the decode an absent key and a key set to its zero
are the same bytes. Those are decided during [LoadSchema], on the merged map,
and they are the reason this domain has a schema rather than a validator.

It is what makes core/app/config.Validator a consumer of this engine rather than
a competitor of it: a struct that wants to keep its own Validate method
implements it in one line, and [LoadSchema] still calls that method after
running the same constraints itself.

	func (c Conf) Validate() error { return appSchema.Check(c).Err() }

The report carries messages the error cannot; the error carries the count,
the first rule and the offending keys. Neither carries a value.

symbols.name: Source
symbols.doc:
Source returns the default LAYER as an ordinary [coreconfig.Source]. It is
exposed so a caller can inspect the effective defaults — printing them for a
`--show-config` flag, or diffing two releases — not so a caller can order
them: [LoadSchema] always merges this layer first, and a default that could
be placed after a file would not be a default.

Each Load returns a fresh copy, so a caller that mutates the map it was
handed cannot change what the next load sees.

symbols.name: Bootstrap
symbols.doc:
Bootstrap founds a cluster on one founding node's log, in phases that are
each idempotent: a bootstrap-pending stamp naming the founding list, the
founding configuration as entry 1, then the member stamp. Every founder
runs it with the IDENTICAL list (D8, R2-24, R3-02, R9-04). It never runs
inside NewNode. Entry 1 carries the generation 1 contract, cfg's
InitialTiming completed and refused as NewNode completes and refuses it:
the contract that rules every node is the one NewNode validates.

symbols.name: ClearQuarantine
symbols.spelled: func(d DataDir, exit QuarantineExit, op coreconsensus.Operator) error
symbols.doc:
ClearQuarantine clears a quarantined, or stopped, directory through one of
the two exits. There is no third exit that keeps the damaged node voting.

fields.name: Cluster
fields.doc: Cluster is the cluster the node belongs to; it must match the stamp.

fields.name: Group
fields.doc: Group is the consensus group, 1 in v1; 0 is clamped to 1.

fields.name: ID
fields.doc: ID is the node; 0 takes the stamp's, any other value must match it.

fields.name: Machine
fields.doc: Machine is the replicated program.

fields.name: Durability
fields.doc: Durability must agree with Machine's siblings.

fields.name: Log
fields.doc:
Log, Snapshots and Transport are the node's ports; the caller owns
them and closes them after the node.

fields.name: Clock
fields.doc: Clock drives every timer; nil is clock.System.

fields.name: InitialTiming
fields.doc:
InitialTiming is proposed at Bootstrap only; the committed contract
rules.

fields.name: SnapshotCodec
fields.doc: SnapshotCodec compresses snapshot chunks; nil is flate.

fields.name: SnapshotPausesApply
fields.doc: SnapshotPausesApply says the state machine cannot cut cheaply.

fields.name: MinVoters
fields.doc: MinVoters is the floor a Remove may not cross.

fields.name: JoinAuthorizer
fields.doc: JoinAuthorizer decides a JOIN; without it every JOIN is refused.

fields.name: HardCloseTimeout
fields.doc: HardCloseTimeout bounds HardClose.

fields.name: Reads
fields.doc: Reads selects the read mode.

fields.name: PreferredLeaders
fields.doc:
PreferredLeaders are the nodes a leader transfers to after an
election when it is not one of them.

fields.name: Seed
fields.doc: Seed draws the election timeouts; 0 draws one.

fields.name: Meter
fields.doc:
Meter, Tracer and Logger receive D13's metrics, one span per Propose
and the role, membership, snapshot and truncation events; nil turns
each off. None of them changes a decision.

symbols.doc:
Config builds a Node. Every bound has a default and a validation (D14): a
zero bound is clamped to its default, and a combination that contradicts
itself is refused with CONSENSUS_MISCONFIGURED.

symbols.name: MemoryBudget
symbols.doc:
MemoryBudget is the node's memory budget with two peers, the sum of its
bounds (D14).

symbols.name: DataDir
symbols.doc:
DataDir is the shipped layout: a lock, a stamp, the segmented log, the
snapshots and the markers. A DataDir value wraps a pointer, so copies
share one lock and one Close (R4-29).

symbols.name: Close
symbols.doc:
Close releases the lock; idempotent, and refused while a Node built on it
is open (R3-18).

symbols.name: Dir
symbols.doc: Dir returns the directory.

symbols.name: Log
symbols.doc: Log returns the directory's LogStore.

symbols.name: Snapshots
symbols.doc: Snapshots returns the directory's SnapshotStore.

symbols.name: DataDirOptions

fields.name: SegmentBytes
fields.doc: SegmentBytes is the fixed size of a log segment; 0 is 64 MiB.

fields.name: RuntimeDir
fields.doc:
RuntimeDir is the boot-scoped directory of the second STORAGE_FAILED
marker (R9-05); empty is /run/kitsunium-consensus on Linux, and
kitsunium-consensus in the temporary directory elsewhere. It must
outlive the process within the boot and be gone at the next one: a
host tmpfs, or systemd's RuntimeDirectory= with
RuntimeDirectoryPreserve=yes. The process must be able to create it
and write in it: NewDataDirWith refuses CONSENSUS_MISCONFIGURED
otherwise, naming the path.

symbols.doc:
DataDirOptions tunes NewDataDirWith: the size of a log segment and the
boot-scoped directory of the second STORAGE_FAILED marker.

symbols.name: DefaultSegmentBytes
symbols.doc: DefaultSegmentBytes is a segment's fixed size (provisional).

symbols.name: Durability
symbols.doc: Durability says where the state machine's state lives (D3).

symbols.name: DurabilityDurable
symbols.doc:
DurabilityDurable is a DurableStateMachine that persists its applied
position with its state.

symbols.name: DurabilityUnset
symbols.doc: DurabilityUnset is refused: the caller states it.

symbols.name: DurabilityVolatile
symbols.doc:
DurabilityVolatile is a state machine held in memory, rebuilt from the
latest snapshot and the log at every start.

symbols.name: HealthFlags
symbols.doc: HealthFlags are a verdict's yes/no answers, one bit each, read with Has.

symbols.name: Has
symbols.doc: Has reports whether every answer of x is set.

symbols.name: HealthHasLeader
symbols.doc: HealthHasLeader is set when a leader is known in the current term.

symbols.name: HealthQuorumReachable
symbols.doc:
HealthQuorumReachable is set on a leader a majority answered within
the minimum election timeout; never elsewhere.

symbols.name: HealthReady
symbols.doc:
HealthReady is the readiness answer: running, a leader known,
everything known committed applied, and not refusing the current
leader's chain (D4).

symbols.name: HealthSnapshotNearLimit
symbols.doc:
HealthSnapshotNearLimit is set when the newest snapshot has reached
four fifths of SnapshotLimit: the cuts are about to be refused
SNAPSHOT_TOO_LARGE (R2-30). Readiness does not depend on it.

symbols.name: HealthStopped
symbols.doc: HealthStopped is set once the node stopped itself or was closed.

fields.name: Status
fields.doc: Status is the node's view after its last turn.

fields.name: Flags
fields.doc:
Flags are the verdict's yes/no answers: HealthReady, HealthHasLeader,
HealthQuorumReachable, HealthStopped, HealthSnapshotNearLimit.

fields.name: FailureTolerance
fields.doc:
FailureTolerance is how many voters can fail now with a majority
left. Only the leader knows it: -1 elsewhere.

fields.name: ApplyLagEntries
fields.doc: ApplyLagEntries is commit minus applied.

fields.name: Peers
fields.doc: Peers is the leader's view of every peer, nil elsewhere.

fields.name: ChainRefusals
fields.doc:
ChainRefusals counts identical chain refusals of this follower at
ChainRefusalIndex from ChainRefusalLeader; the node reports itself
unready while it refuses (D4, R6-05).

fields.name: StopReason
fields.doc: StopReason says why the node stopped itself.

fields.name: DroppedFrames
fields.doc:
DroppedFrames counts frames whose From differed from the
authenticated peer (R7-05).

fields.name: LongTurns
fields.doc:
LongTurns counts the loop turns longer than the drift budget, each of
which dropped the lease (D9, R7-20).

fields.name: JoinsRateLimited
fields.doc: JoinsRateLimited counts JOINs refused by the one-per-slot rate.

fields.name: SnapshotBytes
fields.doc:
SnapshotBytes is the size of the newest snapshot this node holds,
the larger of its encoded and decoded sizes; 0 with none.

fields.name: SnapshotLimit
fields.doc:
SnapshotLimit is the size a cut is held to now: this node's
MaxSnapshotBytes, or the smallest a member announces when lower
(R2-30).

symbols.doc:
HealthValue is a node's verdict for an orchestrator's probe (D13).
HealthReady in Flags is the readiness answer; the other fields say why, and
Peers is filled only on the leader.

symbols.name: ImportObserved
symbols.spelled: func(d DataDir, p *ImportParams, newCluster coreconsensus.ClusterID, members []coreconsensus.MemberValue, opt *RestoreOptions) (coreconsensus.SnapshotMetaValue, error)
symbols.canonical: func(d github.com/kitsunium/sdk/internal/service/app/consensus.DataDir, p *github.com/kitsunium/sdk/internal/service/app/consensus.ImportParams, newCluster github.com/kitsunium/sdk/internal/core/app/consensus.ClusterID, members []github.com/kitsunium/sdk/internal/core/app/consensus.MemberValue, opt *github.com/kitsunium/sdk/internal/service/app/consensus.RestoreOptions) (github.com/kitsunium/sdk/internal/core/app/consensus.SnapshotMetaValue, error)
symbols.doc:
ImportObserved starts a new history on an empty, joining directory from
a saved snapshot and the committed tail an observer read after it: the
tail is checked against the snapshot (consecutive indexes from its
position, terms that never decrease, each payload's BodySum and the
ChainSum chained from the snapshot's ChainTip), replayed through
p.Machine from the snapshot, and the state it reaches is restored as
RestoreSnapshot does, its last entry the index the new history kept. An
empty tail is RestoreSnapshot itself. opt.Expected is the snapshot's
metadata.

A tail that raises the cluster version, changes the timing contract or
the no-space alarm is refused: the restored metadata could not carry it;
import from a snapshot cut after it. Membership entries are checked and
passed over: the new history has its own members.

symbols.name: ImportParams

fields.name: Snapshot
fields.doc: Snapshot is the saved snapshot's encoded stream, as SaveSnapshot wrote it.

fields.name: Tail
fields.doc: Tail is the committed entries read after the snapshot, in log order.

fields.name: Machine
fields.doc: Machine is a fresh state machine; the snapshot is restored into it and the tail applied.

symbols.doc:
ImportParams are what ImportObserved rebuilds a state from: the
snapshot an observer saved, the committed tail it read after it, and the
state machine that replays the one over the other. Snapshot and Machine
are required.

symbols.doc:
Init prepares a joining node purely offline: a random NodeID, a joining
stamp, and the pair the operator or the JOIN gives to AddLearner. It is
idempotent (R3-02, R7-41, R8-10).

symbols.doc:
InitLog prepares a joining log purely offline: a random NodeID, a joining
stamp, and the pair returned. It is idempotent: a log already joining for
that cluster and slot returns its pair (D8, R3-02, R8-10).

symbols.name: Inspect
symbols.doc: Inspect reads a data directory without changing it.

symbols.name: JoinRefusalReason
symbols.doc:
JoinRefusalReason reads the reason a refused JOIN carried back to the
joiner: what the member's JoinAuthorizer chose to say, or the engine's
rule. false when the refusal carried none.

symbols.name: Latest

symbols.name: LeaderHint

symbols.name: MaxJoinReasonBytes
symbols.doc: MaxJoinReasonBytes bounds the reason a JOIN refusal carries to the joiner.

symbols.name: MemoryLog
symbols.doc:
MemoryLog is the in-memory LogStore double (D2): every port contract
except durability, which it has none of. Sync can be made to fail, so a
test drives STORAGE_FAILED.

CompactPrefix implements LogStore; compacting past the end leaves an
empty log at (through+1, through).

MemoryNetwork connects in-memory transports, the double of D2: frames are
copied, delivered on per-lane queues that drop when full, and links can be
cut in either direction.

MemorySnapshots is the in-memory SnapshotStore double. It keeps the
shipped store's contract — a resumable spool, publication at Commit, a

MemoryTransport is one node's end of a MemoryNetwork, the in-memory
double of D2. NewMemoryTransport returns it; Close stops its delivery
until the next Bind.

symbols.name: NewDataDir
symbols.doc:
NewDataDir takes the directory lock FIRST, then reads, scans and repairs
(D11). A second process fails at once with DATA_DIR_LOCKED.

symbols.name: NewDataDirWith
symbols.doc: NewDataDirWith is NewDataDir with options.

symbols.doc: NewMemoryLog returns an empty in-memory log.

symbols.doc: NewMemoryNetwork returns an empty network.

symbols.name: NewMemorySnapshots
symbols.doc: NewMemorySnapshots returns an empty store.

symbols.name: NewMemoryTransport
symbols.doc:
NewMemoryTransport returns the end of the network n that node id sends and
receives through: created on the first call for that id, the same one on
every later call, so a node restarted on the network keeps its links.

symbols.name: NewNode
symbols.doc:
NewNode opens a node over what an offline tool founded or initialised. It
never bootstraps (D8). The start sequence is fixed (D14): the stamp, the
latest snapshot whose checksums pass, the log to its end, then serve.

the CA pool to pass as TransportConfig.Roots.

NewTCPTransport validates the configuration, reads the cluster and slot
from the certificate, and listens (D4, R3-24). It launches the background

is read, never written: the defaults are applied to a copy.

the reloadable identity, its roots included.

symbols.doc:
Node is one member of a consensus group: the event loop that owns the step
function, its storage actor, its apply goroutine and its snapshot
goroutines (D5b). A Node never closes what it was handed.

symbols.doc:
Barrier returns once the local state machine reflects every write
committed before the call (D9).

symbols.name: ClearNoSpace
symbols.spelled: func(ctx context.Context, op coreconsensus.Operator, pre coreconsensus.PreconditionSpec) error
symbols.doc: ClearNoSpace clears the no-space alarm the precondition names.

symbols.name: Close
symbols.doc:
Close transfers leadership first, then stops every goroutine after the
storage actor's final sync (R2-38). It is idempotent.

symbols.name: DenyPin
symbols.spelled: func(ctx context.Context, op coreconsensus.Operator, id coreconsensus.NodeID) error
symbols.doc:
DenyPin withdraws a member's SPKI pin (R9-18). The transport refuses the
member once the change commits. It is refused MEMBERSHIP_INVALID for the
leader itself, and while the voters that answer the leader, the target
left out, are not a majority (R2-27).

symbols.name: HardClose
symbols.doc:
HardClose stops now: no transfer, no final sync, bounded by
HardCloseTimeout (R7-11). It launches one goroutine that waits for the
node's goroutines; when the timeout fires first, that waiter is abandoned
with them and the data directory stays held until the process exits.

symbols.name: Health
symbols.doc: Health returns the node's verdict, computed on the event loop.

symbols.name: Membership
symbols.doc: Membership returns the configuration the node last appended.

symbols.name: Promote
symbols.spelled: func(ctx context.Context, op coreconsensus.Operator, id coreconsensus.NodeID) error
symbols.doc: Promote makes a caught-up learner a voter (D8).

symbols.name: Propose
symbols.doc:
Propose replicates data and returns, once the entry is applied locally,
its token and the value Apply returned. NOT_LEADER means certainly not
appended; OUTCOME_UNKNOWN means it may still commit: read the state through
Barrier before deciding, never retry blindly (D6, R1-04).

symbols.doc: ProposeTimingContract proposes a new timing contract.

symbols.doc: RaiseClusterVersion raises the protocol version every member must speak.

symbols.name: ReadCommitted
symbols.spelled: func(ctx context.Context, from uint64, to uint64, maxBytes int) ([]coreconsensus.EntryValue, error)
symbols.canonical: func(ctx context.Context, from uint64, to uint64, maxBytes int) ([]github.com/kitsunium/sdk/internal/core/app/consensus.EntryValue, error)
symbols.doc:
ReadCommitted returns the committed entries [from, to], to clamped to
what this node's log store holds as committed (its own commit, or the
last entry applied from it), never to the commit the event loop knows
of alone, at most maxBytes of them but always one when any is due.
from below the first entry the log keeps is COMPACTED: the reader
starts again from a snapshot. It reads the log store concurrently
with the writer, as every reader does, and never waits on the loop.

symbols.name: Remove
symbols.spelled: func(ctx context.Context, op coreconsensus.Operator, id coreconsensus.NodeID) error
symbols.doc:
Remove removes a member and retires its id; removing the leader first
transfers leadership (D8).

symbols.name: SaveSnapshot
symbols.spelled: func(ctx context.Context, op coreconsensus.Operator, w io.Writer) (coreconsensus.SnapshotMetaValue, error)
symbols.canonical: func(ctx context.Context, op github.com/kitsunium/sdk/internal/core/app/consensus.Operator, w io.Writer) (github.com/kitsunium/sdk/internal/core/app/consensus.SnapshotMetaValue, error)
symbols.doc:
SaveSnapshot cuts a snapshot now and copies its encoded stream to w, on a
goroutine of its own: once ctx is done it returns, the copy stops at its
next read, and only a write to w already begun may end after the return;
one that blocks keeps that goroutine, and the snapshot pinned, until w
returns.

symbols.name: Status
symbols.doc: Status returns the node's view after its last turn.

symbols.name: StopReason
symbols.doc: StopReason returns why the node stopped itself, if it did.

symbols.name: TransferLeadership
symbols.spelled: func(ctx context.Context, op coreconsensus.Operator, to coreconsensus.NodeID) error
symbols.doc:
TransferLeadership moves leadership to a voter (D8). It records the
operator in an entry, then waits until the target leads or twice the
maximum election timeout passes.

symbols.name: UpdateAddress
symbols.spelled: func(ctx context.Context, op coreconsensus.Operator, id coreconsensus.NodeID, addr string) error

symbols.doc: UpdateAddress changes where a member listens.

symbols.name: WaitApplied
symbols.doc:
WaitApplied returns once the local node has applied t, the entry of t's
term at t's index. A token of another lineage is LINEAGE_MISMATCH. A token
whose index holds an entry of another term is ENTRY_SUPERSEDED, carrying
the token of the entry applied there, or LINEAGE_MISMATCH when it is one of
the predecessor's within the index Recover kept, as is a token of the
predecessor's whose term this node can no longer read there.

symbols.name: Watch
symbols.doc:
Watch implements LeadershipWatcher. Each call launches one goroutine that
closes the returned channel and ends when ctx ends or the node's event
loop stops.

symbols.name: OpenSnapshot
symbols.doc:
OpenSnapshot reads a saved snapshot's encoded stream, as SaveSnapshot
wrote it, without a node: the reader returns the decoded stream, checks
each chunk as it decodes it, bounds the total by opt.MaxDecoded, and
answers SNAPSHOT_CORRUPT instead of io.EOF when the sizes or the SHA-256
differ from opt.Expected's. opt.Codec is, when nil, the codec
opt.Expected names, flate when it names none.

symbols.name: PEMIdentity
symbols.spelled: struct{CertFile string; KeyFile string; CAFile string}
symbols.canonical: struct{CertFile string; KeyFile string; CAFile string}
symbols.doc:
PEMIdentity is a node identity read from PEM files: the certificate (its
chain may follow it), the key, and the consensus CA. It is the
net/tlsid reloadable identity of ADR 0174 D1: GetCertificate rereads the
files when they change, and keeps the old identity when the new one
fails, does not match its key, or carries another key or SAN — a renewal
reuses the key, so the members' pins hold (R8-07). A new CA file is added
to the trusted roots, so a rollover trusts the union.

symbols.name: GetCertificate
symbols.doc:
GetCertificate returns the current certificate, reloading it in place when
its files changed.

symbols.name: ReloadFailures
symbols.doc: ReloadFailures counts the reloads refused so far.

symbols.name: Roots
symbols.doc:
Roots returns the trusted CA pool the identity was read with, the union of
every CA file seen so far, to pass as TransportConfig.Roots.

symbols.name: PeerFlags
symbols.doc:
PeerFlags are a peer's yes/no facts in a health verdict, one bit each,
read with Has.

symbols.name: Has
symbols.doc: Has reports whether every fact of x is set.

symbols.canonical: struct{ID github.com/kitsunium/sdk/internal/core/app/consensus.NodeID; Flags github.com/kitsunium/sdk/internal/service/app/consensus.PeerFlags; Match uint64; Lag uint64; Inflight int; LastContact time.Duration}

fields.doc: ID is the peer.

fields.name: Flags

Flags are the peer's yes/no facts: PeerVoter, PeerUnreachable,
PeerSnapshot.

fields.name: Match

fields.name: Lag
fields.doc: Lag is how far Match is behind the leader's last index.

fields.name: Inflight
fields.doc: Inflight counts the appends in flight to it.

answered in this term.

symbols.doc:
PeerHealthValue is the leader's view of one peer (D13), one line of
HealthValue.Peers. It is taken on the event loop and stale at the next
turn.

symbols.name: PeerSnapshot
symbols.doc: PeerSnapshot is set while a snapshot is being sent to the peer.

symbols.name: PeerUnreachable
symbols.doc:
PeerUnreachable is set when the transport failed to reach the peer
since it last answered, or it has not answered within the minimum
election timeout.

symbols.name: PeerVoter
symbols.doc: PeerVoter is set for a voter, clear for a learner.

symbols.canonical: func[R any](ctx context.Context, r github.com/kitsunium/sdk/internal/core/app/consensus.Replicated, data []byte) (github.com/kitsunium/sdk/internal/core/app/consensus.TokenValue, R, error)
symbols.doc:
ProposeAs types the Apply result. A result of another dynamic type is
RESULT_TYPE_MISMATCH carrying the committed token: the entry IS committed.
A nil result is the zero R.

symbols.name: QuarantineExit
symbols.doc: QuarantineExit is one of the two exits ClearQuarantine allows (R3-09).

symbols.name: ReadIndex
symbols.doc:
ReadIndex confirms every read by a heartbeat round started after it
arrived. It is the zero value and the default.

symbols.name: ReadLease
symbols.doc:
ReadLease serves reads under the leader lease, sound only under the
four conditions of D9; it requires InitialTiming.MaxClockDrift.

symbols.name: ReadMode
symbols.doc: ReadMode selects how Barrier confirms leadership (D9).

symbols.name: ReceiptMessage
symbols.spelled: func(old coreconsensus.ClusterID, next coreconsensus.ClusterID, voter coreconsensus.NodeID) []byte
symbols.doc: ReceiptMessage returns the bytes a witness signs to attest a fenced voter.

symbols.name: Recover
symbols.spelled: func(d DataDir, newCluster coreconsensus.ClusterID, members []coreconsensus.MemberValue, opt *RecoverOptions) error
symbols.doc:
Recover starts a NEW history from this node's log — run it on the
survivor whose report from Inspect holds the highest (LastTerm, Last):
every entry up to its
persisted commit, then the contiguous entries past it whose body and chain
checksums verify and whose term does not decrease, cut at the first that
fails, so no write the old cluster acknowledged is lost;
a new cluster id that records its predecessor and the last index it kept;
and a forced configuration. The audit file records how many entries past
the persisted commit were adopted. Every old voter left out must be
attested fenced by every witness; without witness keys it fails closed.
A stop marker, STOP-RECOVER, is durable before the forced entry and
removed once the new stamp is: a Recover interrupted between the two
refuses a start, and is completed by running Recover again to the same
new cluster, which resumes from the index the first one kept; one to
another cluster is refused. A silence condition TruncateAndStaySilent
left is removed before the marker: the new history is closed to the
terms it guarded, and a silent node never campaigns. An install a crash
interrupted after its snapshot was published is finished first, before
the marker: the new history keeps that snapshot's index, and the forced
entry follows it.

symbols.name: RecoverOptions
symbols.spelled: struct{Confirm string; Operator coreconsensus.Operator; Fenced []coreconsensus.FencedAttestationValue; WitnessKeys []ed25519.PublicKey}

fields.name: Confirm
fields.doc: Confirm must equal the new cluster id in hex: a typed confirmation.

fields.name: Operator
fields.doc: Operator is recorded in the audit file.

fields.name: Fenced
fields.doc: Fenced attests every old voter left out of the new members.

fields.name: WitnessKeys
fields.doc: WitnessKeys verify the receipts: one per witness, each must sign.

symbols.doc:
RecoverOptions are Recover's preconditions (R2-25, R3-02, R4-04, R9-08).
Recover refuses, before it writes anything, an invalid operator, a
confirmation that does not name the new cluster, no witness key, and an
old voter left out without a receipt from every witness.

symbols.name: Redraw
symbols.doc:
Redraw draws a new id, only while the stamp is joining and the log empty,
after a JOIN_REFUSED for a reused or retired id (R8-10).

symbols.name: RedrawLog
symbols.doc:
RedrawLog draws a new NodeID, only while the stamp is joining and the log
is empty (R8-10).

fields.doc:
Last is the last index the directory holds: the log's, or the
newest snapshot's when an install a crash interrupted published it
past the log's end.

fields.name: LastTerm
fields.doc:
LastTerm is the term of the entry at Last, or of the snapshot that
holds Last. With Last it is the key a Recover's survivor is chosen
by: the highest (LastTerm, Last), compared in that order, never Last
alone nor HardState.Term, the term of the last vote.

symbols.doc:
ReportValue is what Inspect reads, read-only: the stamp, the hard state
and bounds of the log, the complete snapshots, and the markers that would
refuse a start.

fields.name: Confirm

fields.name: Operator

differs from Expected.

direction, length-prefixed frames bounded before allocation.

the groups; a member that left has its connections cut and its
handshakes refused from then on (D4).

fields.name: Certificate
fields.doc:
Certificate is the node's certificate and key. It carries exactly one
URI SAN, kitsunium-consensus://<cluster>/slot/<slot>, and both
serverAuth and clientAuth; the transport takes its cluster and slot
from it. GetCertificate, when set, is asked at every handshake instead,
so a renewed certificate over the same key is picked up in place.

fields.name: Roots
fields.doc: Roots is the consensus intermediate, trusted as RootCAs and ClientCAs.

fields.name: ListenAddress
fields.doc: ListenAddress is bound as given, e.g. a private interface (R2-37).

fields.name: Seeds
fields.doc:
Seeds are addresses for the first contact; the committed membership's
addresses rule afterwards.

fields.name: MaxUnauthenticatedPerIP
fields.doc:
MaxUnauthenticatedPerIP caps the connections an IPv4 address, or an
IPv6 /64, may hold before their handshake completes; the addresses
the admitted members' addresses resolve to get ReservedMemberSlots
instead, so a flood never locks a member out (R2-22). It runs before
any TLS byte is read.

symbols.doc:
TransportConfig builds the shipped mTLS transport (D4, D14). A zero bound
is clamped to its default; nil Roots, no certificate, a HandshakeTimeout
above one second, or a control frame bound not below the data bound is
refused.

symbols.name: TruncateAndStaySilent
symbols.doc:
TruncateAndStaySilent truncates at the damage and persists a silence
condition (R4-03).

symbols.name: WipeAndRejoin
symbols.doc:
WipeAndRejoin wipes the directory; the operator then Removes the old
NodeID and Inits under a NEW one (R4-03). A voter's incarnation is
never swapped in place.

fields.doc: ID is this node.

fields.name: Group

fields.name: Log

fields.name: Seed

fields.name: Timing
fields.doc: Timing is the committed timing contract at start.

fields.name: MaxInflight
fields.doc: MaxInflight bounds the appends in flight per peer.

fields.name: MaxInflightBytes
fields.doc: MaxInflightBytes bounds their bytes.

fields.name: MaxBatchBytes
fields.doc: MaxBatchBytes bounds one append.

fields.name: MinVoters
fields.doc: MinVoters is the floor a Remove may not cross.

fields.name: PromoteLag
fields.doc: PromoteLag is how far behind the commit a learner may be promoted.

fields.name: Lease
fields.doc: Lease turns on lease reads.

fields.name: CanVote
fields.doc:
CanVote is false while the directory is joining or silent: such a
node neither votes nor acknowledges.

fields.name: MaxChainRefusals
fields.doc: MaxChainRefusals is N of D4's "no silent loop".

fields.name: NoTable
fields.doc:
NoTable is set while the node holds no usable snapshot: it votes and
stores the log but never campaigns, and asks for a snapshot (R7-18).

fields.name: SilentTerm
fields.doc:
SilentTerm and SilentIndex are the silence condition
TruncateAndStaySilent persisted (R3-09, R4-03): while SilentIndex is
not 0 the node grants no vote and acknowledges no append, until a
leader of a term at least SilentTerm has rewritten its log past
SilentIndex and committed an entry of its own term.

fields.name: SilentIndex
fields.doc:
SilentTerm and SilentIndex are the silence condition
TruncateAndStaySilent persisted (R3-09, R4-03): while SilentIndex is
not 0 the node grants no vote and acknowledges no append, until a
leader of a term at least SilentTerm has rewritten its log past
SilentIndex and committed an entry of its own term.

fields.name: RecentEntriesBytes
fields.doc:
RecentEntriesBytes bounds the payloads held in memory; 0 holds them
all. Older ones are fetched from the store when a peer needs them.

fields.name: MaxEntryBytes
fields.doc:
MaxEntryBytes bounds a forwarded command's payload as the driver
bounds a local one; 0 does not bound it.

fields.name: MaxForwardBytes
fields.doc:
MaxForwardBytes bounds the payload bytes of forwarded commands this
leader appended and has not committed yet; 0 does not bound them.

symbols.doc:

already clamped and validated by the engine.

EngineValue is the engine's own replicated state: the timing contract, the
cluster version and its generation, and the no-space alarm.

symbols.name: FetchSpec
symbols.spelled: struct{To core.NodeID; Lo uint64; Hi uint64}
symbols.doc:
FetchSpec asks for the entries [Lo, Hi) of the store for a peer, whose
payloads the step function evicted. The driver reads them off the event
loop and hands them back with Fetched.

symbols.name: NewRaft
symbols.doc: NewRaft builds the step function over the loaded state.

symbols.name: PeerStatFlags
symbols.doc:
PeerStatFlags are a peer's yes/no facts in the leader's view, one bit
each, read with Has.

symbols.name: Has
symbols.doc: Has reports whether every fact of x is set.

symbols.name: PeerStatValue
symbols.spelled: struct{ID core.NodeID; Flags PeerStatFlags; Match uint64; Next uint64; Inflight int; LastHeard time.Time}
symbols.canonical: struct{ID github.com/kitsunium/sdk/internal/core/app/consensus.NodeID; Flags github.com/kitsunium/sdk/internal/service/app/consensus/raft.PeerStatFlags; Match uint64; Next uint64; Inflight int; LastHeard time.Time}
symbols.doc:
PeerStatValue is the leader's view of one peer, for Health (D13). Flags
say whether it votes, answered in this term, is probed or is being sent a
snapshot; LastHeard is meaningful only once StatHeard is set.

symbols.name: Protocol2
symbols.doc:
Protocol2 is the protocol version whose formats a node writes once the
cluster version is raised to it.

symbols.name: ProtocolMax
symbols.doc:
ProtocolMax is the highest protocol version this engine speaks: a cluster
version above it is refused, and stops a node that finds it committed.
Version 2 adds the snapshot metadata's checksum, the admin payload's
Origin and the log identity's AdoptedFrom, each written only once the
committed cluster version is 2 (lot S3).

symbols.name: Raft
symbols.doc:
Raft is the step function. It is not safe for concurrent use: one event
loop owns it.

symbols.name: ChainAt
symbols.doc: ChainAt returns the chain value at i.

symbols.name: ChainRefusal
symbols.doc:
ChainRefusal names the leader and the index this follower refuses, and
how many times, while it lasts (D4, R6-05).

symbols.name: CheckOffer
symbols.spelled: func(from core.NodeID, o core.InstallOfferValue, needTable bool) errs.Code
symbols.doc:
CheckOffer answers an install offer on the event loop, which alone knows
the term, the leader and the commit index (R8-21). needTable exempts a
node that holds no usable snapshot from the freshness rule (R7-18).

symbols.name: Compact
symbols.doc:
Compact forgets the entries through index, which a durable snapshot
covers.

symbols.name: ConfAt
symbols.doc: ConfAt returns the membership valid at index i.

symbols.name: Debug
symbols.doc: Debug renders the step function's state for a failing test's log.

symbols.name: DropLease
symbols.doc:
DropLease drops the lease for the rest of the term: a loop turn longer than
the drift budget (D9).

symbols.name: EngineAt
symbols.doc:
EngineAt returns the engine's own replicated state as the committed
entries through index i left it: the state a snapshot cut at i carries,
never one an engine entry committed past i set (#402). An index at or
below the log's base answers the state at the base.

symbols.name: Entry
symbols.doc: Entry returns the entry at i, if the step function holds it.

symbols.name: FailureTolerance
symbols.doc:
FailureTolerance is how many voters can fail now with a majority left:
the voters heard within the minimum election timeout, less a quorum. Only
the leader knows it; elsewhere it is -1.

symbols.name: Fetched
symbols.spelled: func(to core.NodeID, lo uint64, ents []core.EntryValue, compacted bool)
symbols.canonical: func(to github.com/kitsunium/sdk/internal/core/app/consensus.NodeID, lo uint64, ents []github.com/kitsunium/sdk/internal/core/app/consensus.EntryValue, compacted bool)
symbols.doc:
Fetched hands back entries read for a peer. Anything stale — another
role, another next, a term the log no longer has at that index — is
dropped, and a compacted read moves the peer to the snapshot path.

symbols.name: HasReady
symbols.doc: HasReady reports whether a turn left work for the driver.

symbols.name: InstallSnapshot
symbols.doc:
InstallSnapshot moves the log onto a snapshot the driver has published and
restored. The suffix after it is kept only when the boundary entry matches
(D7).

symbols.name: LeaseValid
symbols.doc: LeaseValid reports whether the leader's lease holds at now (D9).

symbols.name: NoTable
symbols.doc: NoTable reports whether the node still waits for a snapshot install.

symbols.name: PeerStats
symbols.doc:
PeerStats returns the leader's view of every peer, in configuration
order; nil off the leader.

symbols.name: Progress
symbols.spelled: func(id core.NodeID) (match uint64, lastHeard time.Time, ok bool)
symbols.canonical: func(id github.com/kitsunium/sdk/internal/core/app/consensus.NodeID) (match uint64, lastHeard time.Time, ok bool)
symbols.doc: Progress returns the leader's match index of a peer.

symbols.name: Propose
symbols.doc:
Propose appends entries at the leader. Kind, Version, BodySum and Data are
the proposer's; positions and chain values are assigned here. A refusal
appends nothing.

symbols.name: QuorumActive
symbols.doc:
QuorumActive reports whether a majority answered the leader within the
minimum election timeout.

symbols.name: ReadIndex
symbols.spelled: func(now time.Time, ctx uint64, noLease bool)
symbols.canonical: func(now time.Time, ctx uint64, noLease bool)
symbols.doc:
ReadIndex asks for a linearizable read point under ctx. noLease forces a
confirmation round.

symbols.name: Ready
symbols.doc: Ready returns the work of the turns since the last call and resets it.

symbols.name: ReportUnreachable
symbols.doc: ReportUnreachable moves a peer the transport could not reach to probe.

symbols.name: SetCanVote
symbols.doc:
SetCanVote changes whether the node may vote: a joining directory may once
its admission is appended.

symbols.name: SetOverloaded
symbols.doc:
SetOverloaded tells the state machine whether the driver refuses new
commands for apply backpressure (D6): forwarded ones are refused too.

symbols.name: SnapshotDone
symbols.spelled: func(to core.NodeID, index uint64, ok bool)
symbols.doc:
SnapshotDone ends a snapshot transfer to a peer; index is the snapshot
the driver sent.

symbols.name: SnapshotIndex
symbols.doc: SnapshotIndex returns the base of the in-memory log.

symbols.name: Status
symbols.doc: Status returns the step function's view.

symbols.name: Step
symbols.doc:
Step handles one message. The driver has already checked that m.From is
the peer the transport authenticated (R7-05).

symbols.name: StorageDone
symbols.spelled: func(seq uint64, index uint64, term uint64)
symbols.canonical: func(seq uint64, index uint64, term uint64)
symbols.doc: StorageDone reports that the write seq is durable through (index, term).

symbols.name: TermAt
symbols.doc: TermAt returns the term at i.

symbols.name: Tick
symbols.doc: Tick advances the timers to now.

symbols.name: TransferLeadership
symbols.doc:
TransferLeadership starts a transfer to a voter (D8). It refuses new
proposals from now on and drops the lease for the rest of the term (D9 c).

symbols.name: ReadState
symbols.spelled: struct{Context uint64; Index uint64; Code errs.Code}
symbols.doc:
ReadState answers a read: once applied reaches Index, the read is
linearizable. A non-zero Code refuses it.

symbols.name: ReadyValue
symbols.spelled: struct{Seq uint64; HardState *core.HardState; Commit uint64; TruncateFrom uint64; Entries []core.EntryValue; Messages []core.MessageValue; AfterSync []core.MessageValue; Apply []core.EntryValue; SendSnapshot []core.NodeID; ReadStates []ReadState; Forwarded []core.MessageValue; Transfers []TransferResult; Compact uint64; SilenceEnded bool; Fetch []FetchSpec; Membership []core.MemberValue; LeaderHint core.MemberValue; Unsupported UnsupportedEntryValue; ChainRefusedBy []core.NodeID}
symbols.canonical: struct{Seq uint64; HardState *github.com/kitsunium/sdk/internal/core/app/consensus.HardState; Commit uint64; TruncateFrom uint64; Entries []github.com/kitsunium/sdk/internal/core/app/consensus.EntryValue; Messages []github.com/kitsunium/sdk/internal/core/app/consensus.MessageValue; AfterSync []github.com/kitsunium/sdk/internal/core/app/consensus.MessageValue; Apply []github.com/kitsunium/sdk/internal/core/app/consensus.EntryValue; SendSnapshot []github.com/kitsunium/sdk/internal/core/app/consensus.NodeID; ReadStates []github.com/kitsunium/sdk/internal/service/app/consensus/raft.ReadState; Forwarded []github.com/kitsunium/sdk/internal/core/app/consensus.MessageValue; Transfers []github.com/kitsunium/sdk/internal/service/app/consensus/raft.TransferResult; Compact uint64; SilenceEnded bool; Fetch []github.com/kitsunium/sdk/internal/service/app/consensus/raft.FetchSpec; Membership []github.com/kitsunium/sdk/internal/core/app/consensus.MemberValue; LeaderHint github.com/kitsunium/sdk/internal/core/app/consensus.MemberValue; Unsupported github.com/kitsunium/sdk/internal/service/app/consensus/raft.UnsupportedEntryValue; ChainRefusedBy []github.com/kitsunium/sdk/internal/core/app/consensus.NodeID}

fields.name: Seq
fields.doc: Seq names the write when there is one; completions carry it.

fields.name: HardState
fields.doc:
HardState is set when the term or the vote changed: it is durable
before anything in AfterSync leaves.

fields.name: Commit
fields.doc: Commit is the new commit index, written lazily, 0 when unchanged.

fields.name: TruncateFrom
fields.doc: TruncateFrom removes every entry from that index on, before Entries.

fields.name: Entries
fields.doc: Entries are appended after the truncation.

fields.name: Messages
fields.doc: Messages leave at once.

fields.name: AfterSync
fields.doc: AfterSync leave once this write is durable.

fields.name: Apply
fields.doc: Apply are committed, locally durable entries, in order.

fields.name: SendSnapshot
fields.doc: SendSnapshot names the peers that need a snapshot.

fields.name: ReadStates
fields.doc: ReadStates answer reads.

fields.name: Forwarded
fields.doc: Forwarded are answers to this node's forwarded proposals.

fields.name: Transfers
fields.doc: Transfers end transfers.

fields.name: Compact
fields.doc:
Compact drops the log's prefix through that index, which a durable
snapshot covers.

fields.name: SilenceEnded
fields.doc:
SilenceEnded is set once the silence condition held: the driver
removes it durably.

fields.name: Fetch
fields.doc:
Fetch asks the driver to read entries the step function no longer
holds, off the event loop, and hand them back with Fetched.

fields.name: Membership
fields.doc: Membership is set when the admitted set changed.

fields.name: LeaderHint
fields.doc:
LeaderHint is the leader a member vouched for in a MsgLeaderRecord,
admitted provisionally in Membership, for the driver to log (#542).

fields.name: Unsupported
fields.doc:
Unsupported names an entry whose kind this version does not know:
the driver stops the node with VERSION_UNSUPPORTED.

fields.name: ChainRefusedBy
fields.doc:
ChainRefusedBy names, once per refusal, the leader whose append this
follower refused for a broken chain, for D13's
consensus_chain_refusals_total.

symbols.doc:
ReadyValue is what the driver must do after a turn: write, then send.
Nothing in AfterSync leaves before the write numbered Seq is durable
(D5b).

symbols.name: NeedsWrite
symbols.doc: NeedsWrite reports whether the Ready asks the storage actor for anything.

symbols.name: StartState
symbols.spelled: struct{HardState core.HardState; Snapshot core.SnapshotMetaValue; Entries []core.EntryValue; Applied uint64; Now time.Time}
symbols.canonical: struct{HardState github.com/kitsunium/sdk/internal/core/app/consensus.HardState; Snapshot github.com/kitsunium/sdk/internal/core/app/consensus.SnapshotMetaValue; Entries []github.com/kitsunium/sdk/internal/core/app/consensus.EntryValue; Applied uint64; Now time.Time}

fields.name: HardState
fields.doc: HardState is the last hard state on disk.

fields.name: Snapshot
fields.doc: Snapshot is the base the log continues, zero for none.

fields.name: Entries
fields.doc: Entries are the durable entries after the snapshot.

fields.name: Applied
fields.doc: Applied is where the state machine resumes, at least the snapshot.

fields.name: Now
fields.doc: Now is the start instant: the restart vote-refusal window opens here.

symbols.doc:
StartState is the durable state the driver loaded from its store at
boot. NewRaft rebuilds the step function from it alone, so a restart
depends on nothing held in memory.

symbols.name: StatHeard
symbols.doc:
StatHeard is set once the peer answered in this term; LastHeard is
meaningful only then.

symbols.name: StatProbing
symbols.doc: StatProbing is set while the leader probes for the peer's match.

symbols.name: StatSnapshot
symbols.doc: StatSnapshot is set while a snapshot is being sent to the peer.

symbols.name: StatVoter
symbols.doc: StatVoter is set for a voter, clear for a learner.

symbols.name: StatusValue
symbols.spelled: struct{Role core.Role; Term uint64; Lead core.NodeID; Commit uint64; Last uint64; Stable uint64; Timing core.TimingContractSpec; Cluster uint32; ClusterG uint64; NoSpace core.AlarmID; Conf core.MembershipValue; Committed core.MembershipValue; Transfer core.NodeID}
symbols.canonical: struct{Role github.com/kitsunium/sdk/internal/core/app/consensus.Role; Term uint64; Lead github.com/kitsunium/sdk/internal/core/app/consensus.NodeID; Commit uint64; Last uint64; Stable uint64; Timing github.com/kitsunium/sdk/internal/core/app/consensus.TimingContractSpec; Cluster uint32; ClusterG uint64; NoSpace github.com/kitsunium/sdk/internal/core/app/consensus.AlarmID; Conf github.com/kitsunium/sdk/internal/core/app/consensus.MembershipValue; Committed github.com/kitsunium/sdk/internal/core/app/consensus.MembershipValue; Transfer github.com/kitsunium/sdk/internal/core/app/consensus.NodeID}
symbols.doc:
StatusValue is the step function's part of a node's status. It is a copy:
its memberships are cloned, so the caller may keep it.

symbols.name: TransferResult
symbols.doc:
TransferResult ends a leadership transfer this node started. A zero Code
means TimeoutNow was sent to To; TRANSFER_FAILED means it was not, before
the deadline or before leadership was lost.

symbols.name: UnsupportedEntryValue
symbols.doc:
UnsupportedEntryValue is an entry a leader sent that this version cannot
apply; Index is 0 when there is none.

symbols.name: AdminValue
symbols.spelled: struct{Operator string; Change uint8; Target coreconsensus.NodeID; Pre coreconsensus.PreconditionSpec; Membership coreconsensus.MembershipValue; Contract coreconsensus.TimingContractSpec; ClusterVersion uint32; Origin coreconsensus.NodeID}
symbols.canonical: struct{Operator string; Change uint8; Target github.com/kitsunium/sdk/internal/core/app/consensus.NodeID; Pre github.com/kitsunium/sdk/internal/core/app/consensus.PreconditionSpec; Membership github.com/kitsunium/sdk/internal/core/app/consensus.MembershipValue; Contract github.com/kitsunium/sdk/internal/core/app/consensus.TimingContractSpec; ClusterVersion uint32; Origin github.com/kitsunium/sdk/internal/core/app/consensus.NodeID}

fields.name: Operator
fields.doc: Operator is the identity the caller vouched for.

fields.name: Change
fields.doc: Change is the membership change of an EntryMembership.

fields.name: Target
fields.doc: Target is the node a change or a transfer names.

fields.name: Pre
fields.doc: Pre is the precondition of a clearing or raising operation.

fields.name: Membership
